495	
496	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
497	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
498	
499	Curves change the picture's tones with points on a line. Use **Master** for contrast and the black and white points, and **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** to work on one colour at a time. The picture goes through the curves after the [wheels](/color/wheels/) and before the [look](/color/looks/).
500	
501	<AtAGlance
502	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', 'Esc', '← → ↑ ↓']}
503	  where={['Clip inspector ▸ Color ▸ Curves', 'Right-click a channel cell for Reset']}
504	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
505	/>
506	
507	<Shot
508	  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"
509	  alt="The Curves section open on the Color tab. Six cells read Master, Red, Green, Blue, Hue and Sat, with Master chosen and a dot under Master and Red. Below them a square plot shows a gentle S-curve in black through four points, with the changed Red curve as a faint line behind it. Under the plot are empty In and Out fields and a greyed Delete button."
510	/>
511	
512	## The Curves section
513	
514	Select a video or picture clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts collapsed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".
515	
516	The section has three parts, from top to bottom:
517	
518	- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
519	- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
520	- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.
521	
522	Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.
523	
524	## The channel picker
525	
526	Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click a different cell, and any selected point is deselected.
527	
528	| Cell | What it changes |
529	| --- | --- |
530	| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
531	| **Red** | The red channel only. |
532	| **Green** | The green channel only. |
533	| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
534	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
535	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
536	
537	**Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** are the tone curves, and **Hue** and **Sat** are the hue curves.
538	
539	There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.
540	
541	The chosen cell is framed and labelled in its channel's colour. A new window starts on **Master**, and the plot stays on your channel while the window is open. The choice isn't saved with the project.
542	
543	### See which channels are changed
544	
545	A dot under a cell means that channel has been changed.
546	
547	Changed channels also show as faint lines in their own colour behind the curve you're editing. **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** show behind each other. **Hue** and **Sat** each have their own scale, so neither shows behind the other.
548	
549	## Shape the picture
550	
551	| To | Do this |
552	| --- | --- |
553	| Add contrast | On **Master**, make a gentle S: pull a point low on the curve down, and a point high on the curve up. |
554	| Set the black point | On **Master**, drag the first point right along the bottom. Everything darker than its **In** comes out black. |
555	| Set the white point | On **Master**, drag the last point left along the top. Everything brighter than its **In** comes out white. |
556	| Lift the blacks | On **Master**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
557	| Warm the shadows | On **Red**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
558	| Take out a colour cast | On the channel that's too strong, add a point in the middle of the curve and pull it down. |
559	
560	## Edit points
561	
562	A curve holds from 2 to 16 points. It runs smoothly through every point and never overshoots, so between two points it stays between their values. Past the first and last points, a tone curve stays flat.
563	
564	Each drag, nudge, deletion or typed value is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads **Undo Curves**.
565	
566	### Add a point
567	
568	Click the plot away from any point. Frame Job adds a point on the curve, directly above or below your click, and selects it. Keep the button down and the same press drags it.
569	
570	A double-click on the curve itself adds one point. A double-click away from the curve adds two, side by side, because the second click misses the first point.
571	
572	A 17th point beeps, and so does a click with no room left between two points.
573	
574	On a straight channel, the new point isn't saved until you move it, nudge it or type a value, so a stray click changes nothing. It stays on the plot while it's selected, and it goes when you deselect it or change channel. You can click several in a row to pin a straight curve before you bend it, and they're all saved with the first one you move.
575	
576	On a channel that already has a shape, the click saves the new point straight away. The point lies on the curve, so the picture changes very little, if at all.
577	
578	### Drag a point
579	
580	Press a point to grab it where it stands, with no jump, and drag. It stays inside the plot and can't pass its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.001 on a tone curve and 0.1° on a hue curve.
581	
582	You can drag the end points too.
583	
584	### Fine drag and axis lock
585	
586	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move the point at a tenth of the speed.
587	
588	Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag to lock the point to one axis. It stays put until the pointer has travelled 4 pt from the press, and then whichever direction you moved further wins for the rest of the drag. Let go of <kbd>⇧</kbd> and the point follows the pointer again.
589	
590	<kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⇧</kbd> combine.
591	
592	### Nudge a point
593	
594	With a point selected, the arrow keys nudge it. Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> to go ten times as far. Each press is one undo step.
595	
596	| Channel | Arrow key | With <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
597	| --- | --- | --- |
598	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0.01 | 0.1 |
599	| **Hue** | 1° | 10° |
600	| **Sat** | 1° across, 0.01 up and down | 10° across, 0.1 up and down |
601	
602	### In and Out fields
603	
604	The **In** and **Out** fields below the plot let you type the selected point's position. With no point selected, they're blank and disabled.
605	
606	| Channel | **In** | **Out** |
607	| --- | --- | --- |
608	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0 to 1, three decimals | 0 to 1, three decimals |
609	| **Hue** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | −180° to +180°, one decimal |
610	| **Sat** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | 0× to 2×, two decimals |
611	
612	A number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it, and an **In** past a neighbouring point stops short of that point.
613	
614	### Delete a point
615	
616	Select the point and press <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd>, choose **Delete** below the plot, or double-click the point.
617	
618	A curve can't go below two points. The keys and the double-click beep, and **Delete** is greyed out.
619	
620	### Deselect a point
621	
622	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or click another channel. This also hands the keyboard back to the editor.
623	
624	### The plot and the keyboard
625	
626	While a point is selected the plot has the keyboard, so:
627	
628	- The arrow keys nudge the point rather than move the playhead.
629	- <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the selected clip.
630	
631	Keys the plot doesn't use still reach the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays.
632	
633	## Hover readout
634	
635	While the pointer is over the plot, and during a drag, a small label shows the pointer's position and the curve's value there.
636	
637	| Channel | The label reads |
638	| --- | --- |
639	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | `In 0.42 → Out 0.47` |
640	| **Hue** | `Hue 34° → +12°` |
641	| **Sat** | `Hue 120° → ×0.80` |
642	
643	There's no label outside the plot, and that includes the spectrum strip under a hue channel.
644	
645	## Reset curves
646	
647	To straighten one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat**. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
648	
649	To straighten all six channels, choose **Reset** in the section's header. It shows while a curve is changed, and it's one undo step. You can also right-click the plot and choose **Reset to default**.
650	
651	## Curves inside an action
652	
653	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a curve edit goes to the action's end, so the curve animates. Any two curves animate into each other, whatever their number of points, and so does a curve and a straight line.
654	
655	The plot shows it in its own way: the action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour.
656	
657	To animate a curve back to neutral, right-click a cell and choose its **Reset** item, or right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**. Each writes a straight curve to the action's end, for the channels that aren't already straight. The section's **Reset** isn't there while the action is selected. **Clear** takes its place once the action animates curves, and removes them from the action.
658	
659	See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
660	
661	## Good to know
662	
663	With several clips selected, the plot shows the first clip's curves, and the section shows **mixed** when they differ. An edit gives every selected clip the curve you're editing, for that channel, and leaves their other channels alone.
664	
665	Selecting another clip deselects the point.
666	
667	## With an agent
668	
669	An agent writes a whole channel at once as a list of 2 to 16 points, and that list replaces the channel. Sending `null` for a channel removes its curve, and a list that changes nothing is stored as no curve.
670	
671	A drag stops at a limit, but an agent's value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
672	
673	## Related
674	
675	- [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/)
676	- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
677	- [Looks](/color/looks/)
678	- [Waveform and RGB Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/)
679	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
680	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
681	=== hue-curves
682	---
683	title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
684	description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
685	---
686	
687	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
688	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
689	
690	The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.
691	
692	<AtAGlance
693	  where="Clip inspector ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
694	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
695	/>
696	
697	## The two hue channels
698	
699	The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.
700	
701	| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
702	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
703	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
704	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |
705	
706	So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.
707	
708	Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.
709	
710	The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.
711	
712	## The spectrum strip
713	
714	A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.
715	
716	| Hue | Colour |
717	| --- | --- |
718	| 0° | Red |
719	| 60° | Yellow |
720	| 120° | Green |
721	| 180° | Cyan |
722	| 240° | Blue |
723	| 300° | Magenta |
724	
725	## Hue vs Hue
726	
727	A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.
728	
729	To make the greens more teal:
730	
731	<Steps>
732	
733	1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.
734	
735	2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
736	
737	3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label beside the pointer shows the shift, such as `Hue 120° → +30°`.
738	
739	</Steps>
740	
741	The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.
742	
743	## Hue vs Sat
744	
745	Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.
746	
747	To mute the reds:
748	
749	<Steps>
750	
751	1. With **Curves** open on the clip, click the **Sat** cell.
752	
753	2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
754	
755	3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down. The label beside the pointer shows the gain, such as `Hue 0° → ×0.60`.
756	
757	</Steps>
758	
759	## Hue curve safeguards
760	
761	- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
762	- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
763	- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.
764	
765	## Good to know
766	
767	- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
768	- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
769	- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
770	- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
771	
772	## With an agent
773	
774	An agent writes `hue_hue` and `hue_sat` whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
775	
776	## Related
777	
778	- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)
779	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
780	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
781	- [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/)

1	=== looks
2	---
3	title: "Looks"
4	description: "Put one of eight built-in colour treatments on a clip by picking its thumbnail, set how much of it applies, and take it off again."
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
10	
11	A look is a finished colour treatment you put on a clip in one click and then dial back to taste. It sits on top of your own grade, so it doesn't move the Light, Color, Wheels or Curves controls, and taking it off leaves them as they were.
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu="Clip ▸ Look"
15	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look"
16	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
17	/>
18	
19	## Apply a look
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select one or more clips.
24	
25	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts collapsed.
26	
27	3. Click a tile.
28	
29	4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	<Shot
34	  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
35	  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
36	/>
37	
38	The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.
39	
40	## The Look gallery
41	
42	The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. Each tile is a [thumbnail](#live-thumbnails) of the first selected clip with that look on it, so you choose by eye. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour, and **None** is outlined when no selected clip has a look. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.
43	
44	Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
45	
46	## The eight looks
47	
48	Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls. Most also push a tint into the shadows, the highlights or both.
49	
50	| Look | What it does |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
53	| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
54	| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
55	| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
56	| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
57	| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
58	| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
59	| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |
60	
61	## Live thumbnails
62	
63	Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.
64	
65	The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.
66	
67	A refresh starts about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. That wait begins again each time the frame changes, so the tiles don't refresh while playback or a scrub moves through the clip. They only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.
68	
69	The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.
70	
71	## Amount
72	
73	**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.
74	
75	The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.
76	
77	Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
78	
79	## Remove a look
80	
81	Do any one of these:
82	
83	- Click the **None** tile.
84	- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
85	- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.
86	
87	The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.
88	
89	## Apply a look from the menu
90	
91	**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.
92	
93	A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.
94	
95	The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone. The **Color** sub-tab doesn't show for a selection like that, so the menu is the way to reach the gallery's looks.
96	
97	## The Look summary
98	
99	The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section collapsed.
100	
101	| The header reads | What it means |
102	| --- | --- |
103	| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
104	| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
105	| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |
106	
107	## Looks on stills and adjustment clips
108	
109	A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. The gallery and the menu don't offer one for text, shapes, graphics or nests.
110	
111	On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.
112	
113	## Good to know
114	
115	- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
116	- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
117	- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
118	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
119	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings. See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/).
120	
121	## With an agent
122	
123	An agent sets a look by its kind with `set_video`, for example `{look: {kind: "teal_orange", amount: 0.6}}`, and removes it with `{look: null}`. The kinds are `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic` and `black_white`, and `lut` for an [imported LUT](/color/luts/#with-an-agent).
124	
125	`amount` runs from 0 to 1. Left out, a clip keeps the amount it had, or takes 1 if it had no look. An amount on its own needs a clip that already has a look. A misspelt kind or an amount outside 0 to 1 gives an error and changes nothing.
126	
127	An agent can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. The amount animates, and a change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
128	
129	## Related

134	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)

138	=== luts
139	---
140	title: ".cube LUTs"
141	description: "Bring a .cube colour table into a project, use it as a clip's look, and know what happens when the file changes, goes missing or is removed."
142	---
143	
144	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
145	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
146	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
147	
148	A LUT (look-up table) is a table that turns each colour in the picture into another. Use a `.cube` LUT to bring in a grade from another grading tool, a camera maker or a LUT pack. In Frame Job it's a file in your project, like footage. You add it once, then use it as a clip's [look](/color/looks/), or as the conversion for a [log file](/hdr/log-luts/).
149	
150	<AtAGlance
151	  menu={['Clip ▸ Look', 'File ▸ Add Media…']}
152	  keys="⇧⌘I"
153	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look ▸ Import LUT…', 'Media tab']}
154	  tools={['import_media', 'set_video', 'remove_media']}
155	/>
156	
157	## Import and apply a LUT
158	
159	<Steps>
160	
161	1. Select the clips you want to grade.
162	
163	2. Open the **Look** section of the **Color** sub-tab, and click **Import LUT…** under the gallery. The sub-tab doesn't show if the selection holds a text, shape, graphic or nest clip.
164	
165	3. Choose a `.cube` file.
166	
167	</Steps>
168	
169	<Shot
170	  name="05e-clip-look-lut.inspector"
171	  alt="The Look section with the eight built-in look tiles and None, then an Imported group holding two tiles, Warm Print and Bleach, with Warm Print outlined in blue. The Import LUT… button sits underneath, and the section header reads Warm Print 80%."
172	/>
173	
174	The file joins the project and goes on the selected clips as one undo step, **Import LUT**. If the file is already in the project, Frame Job reuses its entry rather than adding it twice. If Frame Job can't read the file, an error appears and nothing changes.
175	
176	## Add a LUT without applying it
177	
178	Add the file to the project and apply it later:
179	
180	- Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>). A file with the `.cube` extension, in any case, counts as a LUT.
181	- Or drop the file on the **Media** tab. It's the only place in the window that takes a dropped `.cube`.
182	
183	## Apply a LUT already in the project
184	
185	Every LUT in the project is offered in two places, in the order it was added, however the Media tab is sorted:
186	
187	- **The gallery.** Its tile sits in the **Imported** group, in rows of three, and previews the LUT on your frame like any [live thumbnail](/color/looks/#live-thumbnails). The tile's name is the file's name without `.cube`. With no LUTs in the project, the group isn't there.
188	- **The menu.** It's an item in **Clip ▸ Look**, between the eight looks and **None**.
189	
190	Both work as they do for a built-in look, on every selected clip, as one undo step, **Look**.
191	
192	## A LUT is a look
193	
194	A LUT applied to a clip behaves like a built-in look. It comes at the same point in the grade, uses the same [**Amount**](/color/looks/#amount) row, and is removed the same way. A clip that had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with none gets 100%. A clip holds one look, so a LUT replaces a built-in look, and a built-in look replaces a LUT. A LUT also [travels with a paste](/color/copy-a-grade/#luts-travel-with-a-paste) into another project.
195	
196	## LUT rows on the Media tab
197	
198	A LUT appears in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with a cube icon, and its tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."
199	
200	A LUT never goes on the timeline. You can't drag its row, **Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** are off in its right-click menu, and the same commands in the menu bar stay dimmed while its row is selected.
201	
202	The rest of the row works as it does for footage:
203	
204	- **Reveal in Timeline** selects the timeline clips whose look it is.
205	- **Reveal in Finder** shows the file, and **Relink…** points the entry at a new one. A LUT relinks only to another `.cube` file.
206	- **Unused only** leaves out a LUT that a clip's look or a file's Camera Log uses.
207	- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the file into the project with everything else.
208	
209	## Supported .cube files
210	
211	Frame Job reads 3D LUTs in a text `.cube` file of up to 32 MiB.
212	
213	| In the file | What Frame Job does |
214	| --- | --- |
215	| `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65 | Reads it. The line is required, and it comes before the table. |
216	| `TITLE`, `#` comments, blank lines | Reads past them. |
217	| Windows line endings or a UTF-8 byte order mark | Reads them. |
218	| `DOMAIN_MIN 0 0 0`, `DOMAIN_MAX 1 1 1`, `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE 0 1` | Accepts them, because they're the defaults. |
219	| Table values outside 0 to 1 | Accepts them, and clamps them to 0 to 1 when drawing. |
220	
221	Frame Job won't take anything else. It shows an error, usually naming the line it stopped at, and the file stays out of the project. That covers:
222	
223	- A file that isn't text, or is over 32 MiB.
224	- A 1D LUT.
225	- A `LUT_3D_SIZE` outside 2 to 65, or a second `LUT_3D_SIZE` line.
226	- A domain or input range that isn't the default.
227	- A keyword Frame Job doesn't know, or any keyword after the table.
228	- A table with too few or too many rows, or a row without three numbers.
229	- A value that isn't a finite number.
230	
231	The message reads, for example, "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
232	
233	## Warnings in the Look section
234	
235	The section warns you in two cases. Neither stops you, and the LUT still applies.
236	
237	| The warning | When it shows | What it means |
238	| --- | --- | --- |
239	| "This clip's file is converted by Camera Log; a camera LUT here converts it twice." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and its file has a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) setting, or is a PQ HDR file. | A creative LUT is fine there. A camera LUT would convert the footage a second time. |
240	| "This project is HDR (HLG): a .cube LUT reads its values as Rec. 709." | A selected clip's look is a LUT and the [project is HDR](/hdr/dynamic-range/). | The LUT's values keep their 0-to-1 meaning. Frame Job doesn't adapt them for HDR. |
241	
242	## A changed file
243	
244	Frame Job reads the `.cube` file where it is. If you change the file on disk, the new table is read the next time a frame is drawn. There's nothing to import again.
245	
246	## A missing or broken file
247	
248	If the file goes missing, or can't be read any more, the clip draws without its look. The rest of its grade still applies, and the look stays on the clip. A clip's look comes back once the file is back.
249	
250	A missing LUT shows the **missing** badge in the Media tab, and it's in the list Frame Job offers to [relink](/projects/relink-media/) when the project opens. A file that's there but broken has no badge, and the look doesn't draw until you fix the file or relink it.
251	
252	## Remove a LUT in use
253	
254	A LUT counts as used by every clip whose look it is, on the timeline or in a nest, and by every file whose Camera Log it is.
255	
256	<Steps>
257	
258	1. In the Media tab, right-click the LUT's row and choose **Remove**.
259	
260	2. Read the alert, which counts the clips that would lose the look and the files that would lose their Camera Log. For example, "It is the look of 3 clips, which keep their place and lose the look."
261	
262	3. Choose **Remove and Clear Looks**, or **Cancel**.
263	
264	</Steps>
265	
266	**Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT, clears the look from those clips and clears the Camera Log from those files, as one undo step, **Remove Media**. The clips stay where they are. An unused LUT is removed straight away, with no alert.
267	
268	## With an agent
269	
270	An agent adds the file with `import_media`, then applies it with `set_video`, naming the media id `import_media` gave it: `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}`. `media` is required with `lut`, and it's an error with any other kind.
271	
272	An agent can't place a LUT as a clip. `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` and `add_background` give an error that says how to apply it instead. `remove_media` won't remove a LUT in use unless the call sets `with_clips`, which clears those uses as **Remove and Clear Looks** does.
273	
274	An agent can also name a LUT at an action's end. That action stays if the LUT is removed, and draws no look at its end. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/) and [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).
275

284	=== qualifiers
285	---
286	title: Qualifiers
287	description: Limit an adjustment clip's grade to the pixels of one colour or brightness, using hue, saturation and luma ranges.
288	---
289	
290	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
291	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
292	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
293	
294	A qualifier limits an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/)'s grade to the pixels behind it that match up to three ranges of hue, saturation and luma. Use it to change one colour and leave the rest of the picture alone.
295	
296	<AtAGlance
297	  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Qualifier"
298	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'render_frame']}
299	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
300	/>
301	
302	<Shot
303	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
304	  alt="The Qualifier section of an adjustment clip, its header reading hue · sat. Hue is ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30°, Soft 15°, and Saturation at Low 0.15, High 1.00, Soft 0.05. Each strip is dimmed outside its range. Luma is unticked, with a dimmed strip and greyed-out fields. Below are Invert, Blur at 0%, the Pick from Canvas button and a ticked Show Selection."
305	/>
306	
307	## Grade one colour
308	
309	<Steps>
310	
311	1. Put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/#insert-an-adjustment-clip) above the picture, for the span you want.
312	
313	2. With the clip selected, give it a grade in the **Color** sub-tab. A qualifier on its own changes nothing, because it only narrows a grade.
314	
315	3. Open the **Qualifier** section by clicking its header if it's [folded](/getting-started/inspector/#fold-a-section). Press **Pick from Canvas** and click the colour in the preview, or tick a range and set it by hand.
316	
317	4. Tick **Show Selection** to see what's picked. See [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
318	
319	5. Adjust the ranges until the selection is clean, then untick **Show Selection**.
320	
321	</Steps>
322	
323	A qualifier reaches every track behind the clip. To keep it to one area as well, [add a matte](/color/adjustment-clips/#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).
324	
325	## The Qualifier section
326	
327	The **Qualifier** section appears only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip, right after **Adjustment**. A picture clip can't have a qualifier.
328	
329	It holds the three ranges, then **Invert**, **Blur**, [Pick from Canvas](/color/pick-from-canvas/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/).
330	
331	Matching reads the picture behind the clip as it was before the grade, so the grade never changes what it selects.
332	
333	### The Qualifier summary
334	
335	The section's header says what's set: the ranges that are on, then `inverted`, then the blur. For example, `hue · sat · inverted · blur 20%`. It reads `off` when nothing is set.
336	
337	**Reset** appears once anything is set, as long as no action is selected. It turns all three ranges off, clears **Invert** and sets **Blur** to 0 %, as one undo step named **Qualifier**.
338	
339	## Turn a range on
340	
341	Each range has a checkbox, a strip and three fields. Tick the checkbox and the range starts at its default. Ticking or unticking is one undo step named after the range.
342	
343	A range that's off has a dimmed strip that ignores presses, and greyed-out fields, so tick it first. Unticking forgets the range's values: tick it again and it's back at its default.
344	
345	## The three ranges
346	
347	| Range | Picks pixels by | Strip | Fields | Default when ticked |
348	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
349	| **Hue** | Their colour | The colour spectrum, 0 to 360° | **Centre** 0 to 360°, **Width** 0 to 360°, **Soft** 0 to 180°, in whole degrees | Centre 30°, Width 50°, Soft 25° |
350	| **Saturation** | How colourful they are | Neutral to fully saturated | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
351	| **Luma** | How bright they are | Black to white | **Low**, **High** and **Soft**, 0 to 1, two decimals | Low 0, High 1, Soft 0.1 |
352	
353	A number typed outside a field's range is held at the nearest end of it.
354	
355	### Hue range
356	
357	**Centre** is the colour, and **Width** is how much of the spectrum around it is fully picked. **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. The default sits on skin tones: 5° to 55° is fully picked, fading to nothing at 340° and 80°.
358	
359	The band wraps round the spectrum, so a range centred on red picks from both ends of the strip.
360	
361	Greys are never picked by hue, because a grey has no colour to match. A colour fades out of a hue range as it nears grey, from a chroma of 0.06 down to 0.02 on a scale of 0 to 1.
362	
363	### Saturation range
364	
365	This is HSV saturation: 0 is neutral and 1 is fully saturated. **Low** and **High** are the edges of what's fully picked, and **Soft** is the fall-off outside each edge. At its default the range passes everything, so it does nothing until you narrow it.
366	
367	Near-black reads as 0, so dark noise doesn't count as colour. A range that starts above 0 leaves near-black pixels out.
368	
369	### Luma range
370	
371	This is brightness, from 0 for black to 1 for white, measured as Rec. 709 Y′. Its fields work as Saturation's do, and at its default it passes everything too.
372	
373	### Low and High never cross
374	
375	On **Saturation** and **Luma**, a typed **Low** is held at or below **High**, and a typed **High** at or above **Low**. Dragging stops at the same point.
376	
377	## How ranges combine
378	
379	A pixel has to fall inside every range that's on. Tick **Hue** and **Luma** and you get that colour at that brightness, not either one.
380	
381	Each range falls off smoothly across its **Soft** value outside each edge. The partial amounts multiply, so a pixel in the soft edge of two ranges is graded less than one in the soft edge of either. **Soft** at 0 gives a hard edge.
382	
383	## Use a strip
384	
385	Each strip is a live picture of its range, and the quickest way to set it.
386	
387	### Read a strip
388	
389	A strip shows its own scale: the spectrum for Hue, a neutral to red ramp for Saturation, black to white for Luma. It's dimmed 60 % outside the range and 30 % across the soft bands, so what stays bright is what's fully picked.
390	
391	The two block knobs mark the range's edges, and the two small squares mark where the softness runs out.
392	
393	### Drag a strip
394	
395	| Drag | What it changes |
396	| --- | --- |
397	| A block knob | On Hue, the **Width**, evenly about the centre. On Saturation and Luma, the **Low** or **High** edge. |
398	| A small square | **Soft** |
399	| The band between the knobs | Moves the whole range. Hue wraps round. Saturation and Luma stop at the ends of the scale, keeping their width. |
400	
401	A press within 5 points of a handle grabs it, and if a knob and a square are both that close you get the knob. A press outside the band and away from every handle does nothing. When a range runs to the end of its scale, as Saturation and Luma do at their defaults, the square sits on the knob, so use the **Soft** field or narrow the range first.
402	
403	A drag is one undo step named after the range, and so is a number typed into a field.
404	
405	### Drag at a tenth of the speed
406	
407	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move a handle at a tenth of the speed.
408	
409	### Reset a range
410	
411	Double-click a strip to put the range back to its default. It stays on. To turn it off, untick it, or right-click the row and choose **Reset to default**.
412	
413	## Invert
414	
415	Tick **Invert** to grade everything except what the ranges pick. It's off by default. Use it to desaturate everything but one colour, for example.
416	
417	## Blur
418	
419	**Blur** softens the selection, not the picture. On noisy footage a speckled selection turns clean, and the grade blends into its surroundings.
420	
421	| Control | Range | Default |
422	| --- | --- | --- |
423	| **Blur** | 0 to 100 %, a slider and a field with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind its chevron | 0 % |
424	
425	At 100 % the blur is a Gaussian of 24 pixels, measured on the canvas, so a Half or Quarter preview blurs the same share of the picture as an export. It's one undo step named **Qualifier Blur**.
426	
427	Blur never softens a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cutting the clip, and it does nothing while no range is on.
428	
429	## Animate a qualifier
430	
431	An [action](/motion/actions/) can animate a qualifier. Select an action on the clip's action lane, then change a control: the change goes to the action's end, and the numbers ramp there from the values the clip has when the action starts.
432	
433	- **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur** ramp smoothly.
434	- The hue centre takes the short way round the spectrum, so 350° to 10° passes through 0°.
435	- A range turned on or off, and **Invert**, switch at the action's end.
436	
437	While an action animates the qualifier, a strip's band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour. The action holds the qualifier as one setting, so changing any row marks them all. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
438	
439	## Good to know
440	
441	- With several adjustment clips selected, the section shows the first clip's values and a badge marks the rows that differ. A change sends the whole range to every selected clip.
442	- **Invert** with no range on grades nothing, because every pixel counts as picked and Invert takes them all away.
443	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a qualifier only from one adjustment clip to another. A picture clip gets none, and an adjustment clip keeps its own when the attributes come from a picture clip.
444	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), the ranges are measured on the HLG signal and Luma uses BT.2020's weights, so pick them again after switching a project's dynamic range.
445	
446	## With an agent
447	
448	`set_video` sets a qualifier through its `qualifier` key, on adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip.
449	
450	| To | Send as `qualifier` |
451	| --- | --- |
452	| Turn a range on at its default | `{"hue": {}}` |
453	| Change part of a range and keep the rest | `{"hue": {"width": 30}}` |
454	| Turn a range off | `{"hue": null}` |
455	
456	`blur` runs from 0 to 1, where the inspector shows a percentage. A number outside its bounds is an error. It isn't held at the nearest end, as a typed number is.
457	
458	`render_frame` can draw the picture [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) shows, for one adjustment clip, and `set_action_end` animates a qualifier. [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#qualifier) lists every key.

476	
477	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own. For as long as it lasts, it grades everything already drawn behind it, so one grade can cover a whole scene, or a graphic that has no Color tab of its own.
478	
479	<AtAGlance
480	  menu="Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip"
481	  where="Inspector ▸ Clip ▸ Color ▸ Adjustment"
482	  tools={['add_adjustment_clip', 'set_video', 'set_action_end']}

484	
485	<Shot
486	  name="05c-clip-adjustment.window"
487	  alt="The editor with a rose clip named Adjustment selected on its own track, above a video clip on the Video track. The inspector shows only the Color and Clip sub-tabs. Color opens on the Adjustment section with Strength at 75%, then the Qualifier section, which reads off."

489	
490	## What an adjustment clip is
491	
492	An adjustment clip grades every lower track and the canvas background. It never touches a track in front of it, so a title above it stays as it is.
493	
494	On the timeline it's a plain rose block with its name strip and action lane, and no filmstrip. It has no file behind it, so no media length holds it back. Trim or move it to change what it covers.
495	
496	## Insert an adjustment clip
497	
498	<Steps>
499	
500	1. Say what it should cover: set an [In/Out range](/timeline/in-out-range/), or select the clips. With neither, it covers the whole timeline.
501	
502	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**. It has no shortcut.
503	
504	3. Grade in the **Color** sub-tab, which is already open. The new clip is selected and the inspector shows **Clip ▸ Color**.
505	
506	</Steps>
507	
508	The whole thing is one undo step, **Add Adjustment Clip**. The menu item is greyed out while a nest is open, and when the timeline has nothing to cover.
509	
510	### Its span
511	
512	| What's set | What the new clip covers |
513	| --- | --- |
514	| An In/Out range | The range, even if clips are selected too |
515	| Selected clips, no range | From the first selected clip's start to the last one's end |
516	| Neither | The whole timeline |
517	
518	### Its track
519	
520	The new clip goes on the front track when that track has room for the whole span and isn't a matte track. Otherwise Frame Job adds a new front track named **Adjustment** and puts the clip there. A matte front track is never used, because an adjustment clip on one [does nothing](#confine-it-to-part-of-the-picture).
521	
522	A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests. If the clip needs a new track and there are none to spare, nothing is added.
523	
524	## The full grade
525	
526	An adjustment clip's **Color** sub-tab has the same grade a picture clip has, plus two sections of its own at the top. In order:
527	
528	| Section | What it does |
529	| --- | --- |
530	| **Adjustment** | [Strength](#strength), how much of the grade is applied |
531	| **Qualifier** | Narrows the grade to the pixels you pick. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). |
532	| [Light](/color/light/) | Exposure and tone |
533	| [Color](/color/color-section/) | Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue |
534	| [Wheels](/color/wheels/) | Balance shadows, middle and highlights |
535	| [Curves](/color/curves/) | Master, RGB and [hue curves](/color/hue-curves/) |
536	| [Look](/color/looks/) | A built-in look or a [.cube LUT](/color/luts/) |
537	
538	**Adjustment** and **Qualifier** show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip. Select one alongside a picture clip and you get the shared grade sections without those two.
539	
540	### No Picture tab
541	
542	An adjustment clip has nothing to place or crop, so it has no **Picture** sub-tab. Its sub-tabs are **Color** and **Clip**. **Picture** also disappears whenever any adjustment clip is part of the selection.
543	
544	Placement, crop, corners, shadow, reflection and the like can still arrive on one through [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/). They're kept and have no effect.
545	
546	## Strength
547	
548	**Strength** sets how much of the grade is mixed over the picture behind the clip. At 100 % you see the full grade, and at 0 % you see the picture as it was.
549	
550	| Control | Range | Default |
551	| --- | --- | --- |
552	| **Strength** | 0 to 100 %, in whole percent, with presets at 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 behind the field's chevron | 100 % |
553	
554	The section's header shows the current strength. Its **Reset** button returns to 100 %, as one undo step named **Adjustment**.
555	
556	## Fade the grade in or out
557	
558	An adjustment clip can't take a transition, so animate its **Strength** with an [action](/motion/actions/) instead. To fade a grade in:
559	
560	<Steps>
561	
562	1. Select the adjustment clip and set **Strength** to 0 %.
563	
564	2. Put the playhead where the fade should start and press <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd> to [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/). It lasts 1 second, and you can [resize it](/motion/change-an-action/) afterwards.
565	
566	3. With the action selected, set **Strength** to 100 %. The grade ramps there from the Strength the clip has when the action starts.
567	
568	4. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself.
569	
570	</Steps>
571	
572	To fade a grade out, leave the clip's **Strength** where it is, add an action near the end of the clip and set **Strength** to 0 % inside it. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
573	
574	## Confine it to part of the picture
575	
576	An adjustment clip grades the whole frame behind it. There are two ways to narrow that:
577	
578	- **To an area:** put a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) directly in front of the adjustment clip's track. On a track cut by a matte, the clip grades only inside the matte. The matte cuts everything on that track, so keep other clips off it.
579	- **To a colour or brightness:** set a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/). It picks pixels by hue, saturation and luma.
580	
581	The two work together. The grade reaches only the pixels both allow, mixed at the clip's Strength.
582	
583	The adjustment clip must not sit on the matte track itself. There it has no effect, and the inspector says "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect."
584	
585	## Grade a graphic
586	
587	[Graphics](/graphics/graphic-tab/) have no **Color** sub-tab, and neither do text, shapes or nests. To grade one, put an adjustment clip above it for the span you want. Select the clip first and **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** matches its span, unless an In/Out range is set. The adjustment clip grades every track behind it, so add a matte if other tracks show through.
588	
589	## Limits
590	
591	### No nests
592	
593	An adjustment clip can't go inside a nest. **Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip** is greyed out while one is open, Frame Job won't [nest](/editing/nests/) a selection that holds an adjustment clip, and pasting one into an open nest fails. Inside a nest it would grade the layers behind the nest clip as well as the nest's own.
594	
595	To grade a nest, put an adjustment clip above the nest clip on the timeline.
596	
597	### No transitions or overlaps
598	
599	An adjustment clip can't take a [transition](/motion/transitions/), and it can't overlap another clip on its track, because an overlap is a transition. Frame Job won't make the edit, so [fade its Strength](#fade-the-grade-in-or-out) instead. Two clips that only touch are fine.
600	
601	### No blur, sharpen, pixelate or blend modes
602	
603	These need pixels or a colour of the clip's own, and an adjustment clip has neither. If [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) would bring one onto an adjustment clip, nothing is pasted.
604	
605	The point [filters](/effects/filters/), **Sepia**, **Noir**, **Vignette** and **Invert**, do work, and apply to the picture behind it. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so they reach it through Paste Attributes or an agent.
606	
607	## Good to know
608	
609	- A clip with no grade set changes nothing, and neither does a qualifier on its own. A qualifier narrows a grade, so there has to be one.
610	- **Clip ▸ Speed…**, **Clip ▸ Speed Ramp…** and **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background** are dimmed for an adjustment clip, and its **Clip** sub-tab has no [Speed](/speed/speed-section/) section, because it has no source and no picture size. [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) still stretches or squeezes one inside its range.
611	
612	## With an agent
613	
614	`add_adjustment_clip` places a clip on the `track` and `at` the time you name, and it lasts 5 seconds unless you give a `duration`. It doesn't work out a span or a track as the menu does, so an agent can put one on a matte track, where it does nothing. It won't add one while a nest is open.
615	
616	`set_video` then grades it with everything the Color tab offers, and can also give it point filters directly. To an agent, Strength is the clip's `opacity`, from 0 to 1, and `set_action_end` animates it. A blur, sharpen or pixelate filter or a blend mode is an error, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter". See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/) and [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
617

626	=== animate-a-grade
627	---
628	title: "Animate a grade"
629	description: "Put a grade inside an action so it changes over time: what ramps, what switches at the end, how each control shows it, and how to take it back out."
630	---
631	
632	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
633	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
634	
635	Most grade settings can change over time. Put a change inside an [action](/motion/actions/) and a shot can warm up as the sun comes out, drain to black and white, or ease into a new contrast curve.
636	
637	<AtAGlance
638	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
639	  keys="⌥⌘K"
640	  where={['Clip tab ▸ action lane', 'Clip tab ▸ Color']}
641	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_video']}
642	/>
643	
644	## Grade inside an action
645	
646	<Steps>
647	
648	1. Select the clip and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/), or [select one](/motion/select-an-action/) on its action lane.
649	
650	2. Open the **Clip** tab's **Color** sub-tab.
651	
652	3. Change a control. The change goes to the action's end state, and the value ramps there from where it stands when the action starts.
653	
654	4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to watch the grade travel.
655	
656	</Steps>
657	
658	Light, Color, Wheels, Curves and the look's **Amount** can all animate, and on an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) so can **Strength** and the [Qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
659	
660	While the action is selected, every control shows the value at the action's end. When you're done, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to go back to editing the clip itself. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/) for how an action's end state works in every tab.
661	
662	:::tip
663	An adjustment clip can't take a transition. To fade a grade in, set its **Strength** to 0 % on the clip, then add an action and raise **Strength** to 100 %.
664	:::
665	
666	## What ramps smoothly
667	
668	These move gradually from the start value to the end value, along the action's [easing curve](/motion/actions/#easing-curves):
669	
670	- every slider in **Light** and **Color**
671	- each wheel's colour push and master in **Wheels**
672	- the look's **Amount**
673	- **Strength** on an adjustment clip
674	- the Qualifier's numbers: **Centre**, **Width**, **Soft**, **Low**, **High** and **Blur**
675	
676	## Curves animate
677	
678	Curves in an action always animate, on all six channels, including **Hue** and **Sat**. An edit to a curve goes to the action's end even when you add or delete a point.
679	
680	| The two curves | How they animate |
681	| --- | --- |
682	| Same number of points | They ramp point by point |
683	| One is a straight line | The straight one lines up with the other curve's points, then they ramp point by point |
684	| Different numbers of points | Their values blend over the action, from the first curve's result to the second's |
685	
686	### Animate a curve back to neutral
687	
688	To have a curve straighten out over the action, write a straight curve to its end:
689	
690	- For one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Red**, or whichever channel it is. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
691	- For every channel, right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**.
692	
693	The section's **Reset** isn't there while an action is selected. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/).
694	
695	## A look switches instead
696	
697	Turning a look on or off, or changing it, applies to the clip itself and not to the action, even with an action selected. A look tile, **None** and **Clip ▸ Look** all change the clip's own look, as one undo step called Look, and the change shows across the whole clip.
698	
699	**Amount** is what animates. To fade a look in, choose the look and set **Amount** to 0 % with no action selected, then select an action and raise **Amount**. The Amount row only shows once the clip has a look, so choose the look first.
700	
701	## Animate a qualifier
702	
703	A qualifier's numbers ramp, but a range itself can't fade in or out.
704	
705	### A qualifier range switches
706	
707	Ticking **Hue**, **Saturation** or **Luma** with an action selected turns that range on at the action's end. It has nothing to ramp from, so it stays off through the action and then appears whole, at the end values you set. **Invert** switches at the end too.
708	
709	If the clip has no qualifier at all when the action starts, the whole qualifier appears at the action's end, and its **Blur** doesn't ramp either.
710	
711	An action can't turn off a range the clip already has on. Unticking a box with an action selected only takes that range back out of the action. To turn a range off, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> and untick it on the clip.
712	
713	### A hue centre takes the short way
714	
715	An animated **Centre** goes the short way round the colour wheel, so 350° to 10° passes through 0° and never visits the greens and blues. Two centres exactly 180° apart have no short way, so the number moves straight from one to the other.
716	
717	## See what the action animates
718	
719	Row marks and the tab badge show what the selected action does to the grade.
720	
721	- **◆** in a row's gutter means the selected action animates that row. See [Read the row marks](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) for all the marks.
722	- **◆N** on the **Color** sub-tab counts how many grade settings the action animates.
723	
724	The badge counts settings, not values. Each of these counts as one, however many values inside it change:
725	
726	- Light and Color, together, for all thirteen sliders
727	- Wheels
728	- Curves
729	- Look
730	- Qualifier
731	- Strength, on an adjustment clip
732	
733	The same grouping decides the marks. All thirteen Light and Color sliders show ◆ as soon as the action changes one of them, and every Qualifier row does as soon as the action changes any part of the qualifier. The Qualifier's range rows and **Invert** read "at end" whenever that happens, even for a range whose numbers are ramping.
734	
735	## Take a setting back out
736	
737	| To | Do this |
738	| --- | --- |
739	| Take a row out of the action | Hover over its ◆ and click the ×, or right-click the row and choose **Remove from action N** |
740	| Take a section out of the action | Choose **Clear** in the section's header |
741	| Make the row animate to its default | Right-click the row and choose **Set end value to default** |
742	| Put a row back to its default on the clip itself, with no action selected | Right-click the row and choose **Reset to default** |
743	
744	**Clear** takes the place of **Reset** in a grade section's header while an action is selected, and shows only when the action animates one of that section's rows.
745	
746	The default items are greyed out while the row already holds its default. Text fields and pop-ups keep their own right-click menus, so right-click a row's label, its slider or its gutter. On **Wheels** and **Curves** the whole section is one row, so these items act on all of it.
747	
748	:::caution
749	Light and Color are one setting inside an action, so **Remove from action N** on any slider takes all thirteen out, and so does **Clear** on either section. To change one slider back, use **Set end value to default**, or type a new end value.
750	:::
751	
752	## How each control shows an action
753	
754	| Control | While the action animates it |
755	| --- | --- |
756	| Slider | The same marks as everywhere else in the inspector. See [See the value change as it plays](/motion/edit-an-action/#see-the-value-change-as-it-plays) |
757	| Wheel disc | A hollow square at the action's start value, the puck in the action colour, and a coral mark at the value under the playhead |
758	| Wheel strip | The strip fills in the action colour from the start value, the knob is in the action colour, and a coral tick marks the playhead's value |
759	| Curve plot | The action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour |
760	| Qualifier strip | The band is outlined and its knobs are drawn in the action colour |
761	
762	The coral marks show only when the playhead is on the clip and the value there differs from the end value. A qualifier's hue band that wraps past 0° gets its knobs in the action colour but no outline. The three wheels are one row, so all three discs and strips count as animated as soon as the action changes any one of them.
763	
764	## With an agent
765	
766	An agent uses `add_action`, then `set_action_end` with the end values in its `video` group: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look.amount`, and on an adjustment clip `qualifier` and `opacity`, which is **Strength**. It changes the clip's own look with `set_video`. It can do one thing the Color tab can't: name a different look in an action's end. A look or LUT that differs between the start and the end switches at the action's end, **Amount** included. **Amount** ramps only while the look stays the same. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).
767	
768	## Related

772	- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
773	- [Wheels](/color/wheels/)
774	- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)

778	=== copy-a-grade
779	---
780	title: "Copy a grade"
781	description: "Give other clips the grade you built on one clip, what comes with it, how LUTs and qualifiers travel, and what stops a paste."
782	---
783	
784	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
785	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
786	
787	When one clip looks right, Paste Attributes gives its grade to any number of other clips in one undo step. This page covers what that means for a grade. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) covers the command in full.
788	
789	<AtAGlance
790	  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Attributes"
791	  keys={['⌘C', '⌥⌘V']}
792	  tools={['paste_attributes', 'paste']}
793	/>
794	
795	## Copy a grade with Paste Attributes
796	
797	<Steps>
798	
799	1. Select the graded clip and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.
800	
801	2. Select the clips that should take the grade.
802	
803	3. Press <kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>, or choose **Edit ▸ Paste Attributes**.
804	
805	</Steps>
806	
807	The copied clip's video settings replace each selected clip's, as one undo step called Paste Attributes. If nothing would change, Frame Job beeps.
808	
809	## What comes with the grade
810	
811	There's no way to paste the grade alone, because it travels with the rest of the clip's picture settings:
812	
813	- Light, Color, Wheels, Curves, and the look with its **Amount**
814	- filters
815	- everything else about the picture, including position and scale
816	- the audio settings too, where the copied clip has sound and the target can take them
817	
818	A clip's place, speed, actions, transitions, name and label never come across.
819	
820	:::caution
821	Position and scale come with the grade. Pasting onto a clip you've already placed moves it to where the copied clip sits. To share a grade without touching placement, put an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) above the clips instead.
822	:::
823	
824	The paste replaces, it doesn't merge, so anything the target had that the copied clip didn't is gone. A grade that lives in an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) doesn't travel either, because actions stay behind. The target takes the copied clip's own values, not its animation.
825	
826	## LUTs travel with a paste
827	
828	A look that uses an imported [`.cube` LUT](/color/luts/) keeps working when you paste it into another project, with Paste Attributes or with **Edit ▸ Paste**. The LUT arrives in that project's media along with the clip, and if the project already has the same file, the paste uses that one.
829	
830	A pasted look never lands on the wrong file. If what's being pasted doesn't carry the LUT, the clip gets no look.
831	
832	## A qualifier between clips
833	
834	A [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) belongs to an adjustment clip, so what happens to it depends on the clips at both ends of the paste.
835	
836	| Pasting | The qualifier |
837	| --- | --- |
838	| Onto an ordinary clip | Is dropped |
839	| From an ordinary clip onto an adjustment clip | Stays as the adjustment clip had it |
840	| From one adjustment clip onto another | Is copied |
841	
842	## When a paste stops
843	
844	An adjustment clip has no picture of its own, so some settings can't land on it. If the copied clip has a blur, sharpen or pixelate filter, or a blend mode, pasting onto an adjustment clip shows an error naming the clip and the setting, and nothing changes on any selected clip.
845	
846	Sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters paste onto an adjustment clip without trouble.
847	
848	To get past it, take the setting off the copied clip and copy it again, or leave the adjustment clip out of the selection. [When a paste stops](/editing/paste-attributes/#when-a-paste-stops) has the full list, for every kind of clip.
849	
850	## With an agent
851	
852	The menu item always copies each of the picture, sound, text and shape groups both clips have. An agent can list the ones it wants in `paste_attributes`'s `groups`, out of `video`, `audio`, `text`, `shape` and `graphic`, so `["video"]` brings the picture settings and leaves the sound alone. The grade is still part of `video`, so to set a grade and nothing else, an agent uses `set_video`. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).
853	
854	## Related

858	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)

862	=== pick-from-canvas
863	---
864	title: "Pick from Canvas"
865	description: "Click a colour in the preview to centre an adjustment clip's qualifier on it, instead of finding it on the range strips."
866	---
867	
868	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
869	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
870	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
871	
872	Pick from Canvas aims a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) at a colour you can see. You click the picture and the ranges centre on that colour, so you don't have to find it on the strips by hand. The [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/#pick-from-canvas) has an eyedropper of its own, with the same name.
873	
874	<AtAGlance
875	  where="Color tab ▸ Qualifier ▸ Pick from Canvas"
876	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
877	  needs="Every selected clip must be an adjustment clip."
878	/>
879	
880	<Shot
881	  name="05h-clip-qualifier.inspector"
882	  alt="The Qualifier section of the Color tab, with Hue ticked at Centre 25°, Width 30° and Soft 15°, Saturation ticked at Low 0.15, High 1.00 and Soft 0.05, Luma unticked, and the Pick from Canvas button beside a ticked Show Selection."
883	/>
884	
885	## Pick a colour
886	
887	<Steps>
888	
889	1. Select the [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), and move the playhead to a frame that shows the colour. The **Qualifier** section only appears while every selected clip is an adjustment clip. For any other selection the button beeps and no pick starts.
890	
891	2. In the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open the **Qualifier** section and press **Pick from Canvas**. The pointer becomes a crosshair over the preview, and a hint reads "Click to pick the colour to qualify · Esc to cancel".
892	
893	3. Click the colour in the preview.
894	
895	</Steps>
896	
897	The ranges move to that colour, and the pick ends. It's one undo step, named Qualifier.
898	
899	Frame Job reads the colour from the picture behind the adjustment clip, at the playhead. The clip's own grade and every layer in front of it are left out. So the colour you get is the one the qualifier will really test, even after your grade has changed how it looks, and clicking a title on top samples what's underneath it.
900	
901	Turn on [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) to check what the pick caught.
902	
903	## What a pick sets
904	
905	| Range | If it was off | If it was on |
906	| --- | --- | --- |
907	| **Hue** | Turns on, centred on the colour, 30° wide with 15° softness. | Moves its centre to the colour. |
908	| **Saturation** | Turns on, centred on the colour's saturation, 0.3 wide with softness 0.1. | Moves to centre on the colour's saturation. |
909	| **Luma** | Stays off. | Moves to centre on the colour's brightness. |
910	
911	A range that was already on keeps its width and softness, so you can set how wide you want a range and then pick again to move it. **Invert** and **Blur** don't change.
912	
913	If you click a near-grey, there's no real hue to aim at, so **Hue** turns off. A near-grey here is a colour whose strongest and weakest channels are less than 0.06 apart, on a scale of 0 to 1. **Saturation** still turns on and centres, which is how you pick the greys in a picture.
914	
915	**Saturation** and **Luma** stay inside 0 to 1. A range that would cross either end is shifted back inside at its full width, so it's no longer centred on the colour, but the colour stays inside it.
916	
917	## Pick inside an action
918	
919	With an [action](/motion/select-an-action/) selected, the picked ranges go to the action's end state instead of the clip, as any qualifier control does. The width and softness a range keeps are the ones the section is showing. Clicking a near-grey takes **Hue** out of the end state rather than turning it off, so if the clip itself has **Hue** on, it stays on. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
920	
921	## Cancel a pick
922	
923	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or press **Pick from Canvas** again. Changing the selection cancels the pick too. Nothing in the qualifier changes.
924	
925	A click in the area around the picture beeps and the pick stays on, so you can click again.
926	
927	## Good to know
928	
929	- Only one tool that waits for you on the preview can be on at a time. Starting Pick from Canvas cancels any other, such as the chroma key's eyedropper or a [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) drag, and starting one of those cancels a pick.
930	- If the playhead isn't on the adjustment clip, no layers are left out, so you sample the frame as it's drawn.
931	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) don't change what you sample. A pick reads the real picture, whatever the preview is showing.
932	- With several adjustment clips selected, Frame Job samples behind the first and writes the same ranges to all of them.
933	- In an HDR (HLG) project, a pick reads the HLG values, which are what the qualifier tests.
934	- If the selection changes while Frame Job is sampling, it beeps and changes nothing.
935	
936	## With an agent
937	
938	No agent tool clicks the canvas. An agent writes the ranges itself with `set_video`, or with `set_action_end` for an action's end state. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
939	
940	## Related

944	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)

2	---
3	title: "Blending: encoded or linear light"
4	description: "Choose how layers mix where they overlap, so a dissolve between saturated clips keeps its brightness and a glow adds light the way light does."
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	
10	Blending sets how layers mix wherever they overlap: in opacity, dissolves, soft edges, blend modes and glows. Most projects can stay on **Encoded**. Choose **Linear light** when a dissolve between saturated clips dips dark at its midpoint.
11	
12	<AtAGlance where="Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Blending" tools="set_canvas" />
13	
14	## The Blending popup
15	
16	<Steps>
17	
18	1. Open the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).
19	
20	2. In the **Canvas** section, choose **Encoded** or **Linear light** from **Blending**.
21	
22	</Steps>
23	
24	Blending belongs to the whole project and works in SDR and HDR (HLG) projects alike. Every project starts on **Encoded**. The preview, saved frames and exports all follow the setting.
25	
26	The change is one undo step, **Blending**. Choosing the item that's already set changes nothing and adds no undo step. The popup still works with a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, because it's about the project and not the nest.
27	
28	## Encoded
29	
30	Layers blend on their encoded values: the numbers the picture is stored as, which follow a brightness curve and don't measure light directly. Most editors blend this way, and it's the default for every project.
31	
32	## Linear light
33	
34	Layers blend as light. Each layer is decoded after its grade, the layers are blended, and the result is encoded once on the way out. You'll see these differences:
35	
36	- A dissolve between two saturated clips keeps its brightness instead of dipping dark at the midpoint.
37	- A title fading over video comes out brighter.
38	- A blurred or feathered edge comes out brighter.
39	- A glow adds light the way light does.
40	
41	In an HDR (HLG) project, "linear" means HLG's scene light: the light in the scene, before HLG's curve is applied.
42	
43	## What it leaves alone
44	
45	Blending changes no clip and no grade. Layers are graded before they blend, so a grade looks the same either way.
46	
47	These all read the same values on either setting:
48	
49	- Grades
50	- The chroma key
51	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/) and [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/)
52	- Luma [mattes](/canvas/matte-tracks/), which cut what they cut before
53	- The [scopes](/color/scopes/), which still measure the finished, encoded picture
54	
55	## With an agent
56	
57	`set_canvas` makes the same choice, with `blending` set to `encoded` or `linear`. It changes the whole project, so it won't run on a call addressed to a nest, where a person can still use the popup. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
58	
59	## Related
