2	title: "Histogram"
3	description: "See how a frame's tones are spread from black to white, and read how much of the picture is clipped at each end."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The histogram shows how a frame's tones are spread: how much of the picture is dark, how much is bright, and whether either end has run out of room. Use it to judge exposure and contrast, and to catch clipping while you grade.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
12	  keys="⌃⌘W"
13	  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's pop-up ▸ Histogram"
14	  tools="render_frame"
15	/>
16	
17	## Open the histogram
18	
19	Choose **View ▸ Scopes**, then pick **Histogram** from a slot's pop-up. Neither slot opens on it, because a new window starts with **Waveform** over **Vectorscope**. The choice lasts while the window is open. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.
20	
21	## Read the histogram
22	
23	Levels run from 0 on the left to 255 on the right, so black is at the left edge and white is at the right. The height at each level is how many pixels sit there.
24	
25	Red, green and blue are drawn as translucent tinted fills, and luma, the picture's brightness, is a white line on top.
26	
27	| What you see | What it tells you |
28	| --- | --- |
29	| A pile against the left edge | Shadows are crushed to black |
30	| A pile against the right edge | Highlights are clipped to white |
31	| Empty space at both ends | A flat picture, with room to add contrast in [Light](/color/light/) or [Curves](/color/curves/) |
32	| One colour's fill sitting to the side of the others | That channel is brighter or darker overall, which often means a colour cast |
33	
34	Heights are on a logarithmic scale, so a small count still shows up beside a big one, and a peak twice as tall holds far more than twice the pixels. All four share one scale, set by the tallest count in any of them, so you can compare them directly.
35	
36	## Clipping readouts
37	
38	Two readouts sit below the histogram:
39	
40	- **Highlights clipped** is the share of the frame at the very top level, 255.
41	- **Shadows clipped** is the share at the very bottom level, 0.
42	
43	They read like "Highlights clipped 1.9 %", to one decimal place, and show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) shows the same two figures.
44	
45	Both are measured on luma, so read them with these in mind:
46	
47	- A single colour channel can clip while luma doesn't. Watch the fills at the right edge, or use the [Parade](/color/waveform-and-parade/), to catch that.
48	- They count the whole frame. Black canvas around a smaller picture, or letterbox bars, counts towards **Shadows clipped**.
49	
50	## Good to know
51	
52	- The histogram measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
53	- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values. In an HDR (HLG) project it reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and luma is worked out for that colour space. With **Show SDR Version** on, the scope reads that SDR picture as it would in an SDR project. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
54	- The histogram is 140 pt tall. If the preview area is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them. Under 360 pt tall, only the top slot shows.
55	
56	## With an agent
57	
58	`render_frame` measures a frame's histogram as numbers when an agent passes `histogram: true`, which is off by default. The reply says what share of the frame clips high and low by luma. The counts for red, green, blue and luma at each of the 256 levels, and both percentages, go to a `.histogram.json` file beside the image. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
59

2	title: "Vectorscope"
3	description: "Read the hues in a frame and how strong they are, spot a colour cast, check skin tones against the skin line, and zoom in on a low-saturation picture."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The vectorscope shows a frame's colour with its brightness taken away: which hues are in the picture and how strong they are. Use it to spot a colour cast, to check skin tones, and to see how far a grade has pushed saturation.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
14	  keys="⌃⌘W"
15	  where="The Scopes panel ▸ a slot's pop-up ▸ Vectorscope"
16	  tools="render_frame"
17	/>
18	
19	<Shot
20	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
21	  alt="The preview with the Scopes panel beside it. The bottom slot shows the Vectorscope, a near-black square with six labelled target boxes around it, R at the top, Mg top right, B right, Cy at the bottom, G bottom left and Yl left. A line runs from the centre cross up and to the left, and a thin white trace runs from the centre towards the B box, for the blue card in the picture. The 1×, 2× and 4× cells sit in the bottom-right corner, with 1× filled."
22	/>
23	
24	## Open the vectorscope
25	
26	Choose **View ▸ Scopes**. In a new window the panel starts with **Waveform** on top and **Vectorscope** below. If a slot shows something else, pick **Vectorscope** from its pop-up. Both slots can show it, each at its own zoom. See [Scopes](/color/scopes/) for the panel itself.
27	
28	## Read the trace
29	
30	Every pixel in the frame lands somewhere on the near-black square, and the white trace is all of them together.
31	
32	- **The centre is no colour.** Greys, black and white all sit on the faint cross.
33	- **Distance from the centre is strength.** A pale colour stays close in, and a saturated one reaches out towards the edge.
34	- **Direction is hue.** The [targets](#the-targets) show which way each colour lies.
35	- **Brightness is how many pixels are there.** The scale is logarithmic, so a small patch of colour still shows up beside a large one.
36	
37	The two axes are the colour-difference signals: Cb runs across and Cr runs up. The scope draws no circles and has no readouts, so the targets and the skin line are your only references.
38	
39	A picture with no colour cast keeps its neutral areas on the cross. If something that should be grey sits to one side of it, the picture leans the way the trace leans. [Zoom in](#zoom-in-on-a-low-saturation-picture) to see a small cast.
40	
41	## The targets
42	
43	Six boxes mark where 75 % colour bars land, so you can tell which way a colour lies and how strong it is. Each label sits outside its box, away from the centre.
44	
45	| Label | Colour | Where it sits |
46	| --- | --- | --- |
47	| R | Red | Up, a little left |
48	| Mg | Magenta | Up and right |
49	| B | Blue | Right, a little down |
50	| Cy | Cyan | Down, a little right |
51	| G | Green | Down and left |
52	| Yl | Yellow | Left, a little up |
53	
54	## The skin line
55	
56	The line running out from the centre, up and to the left, marks where skin tones fall. It's drawn at the hue of a standard light-skin reference colour, 123.3° anticlockwise from the right.
57	
58	Skin has a similar hue across complexions, and mostly differs in brightness and strength. If the trace from a face sits well to one side of the line, the picture has a cast.
59	
60	## Zoom in on a low-saturation picture
61	
62	The **1×**, **2×** and **4×** cells in the scope's bottom-right corner zoom in around the centre, to show small casts in a picture with little colour in it. Click a cell to choose it. The filled cell is the current zoom.
63	
64	Frame Job counts the pixels again at each zoom instead of enlarging the picture of the trace, so a magnified trace stays sharp.
65	
66	At 2× and 4×, a pixel too strong to fit on the square is left off, and it isn't piled up against the edge. At 1× everything fits.
67	
68	All six targets are too far out to fit at 2× and 4×. Each one becomes a 6 pt tick on the rim that points towards it, with its label inside the rim.
69	
70	Each slot keeps its own zoom when you pick another scope and come back, and when you hide the panel and show it again. A zoom lasts while the window is open. It isn't saved, and every slot starts at 1× in a new window. A cell works on the first click, even when its window isn't the active one.
71	
72	## Good to know
73	
74	- The scope measures the frame the preview composes, so it follows playback, your edits and [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/). It changes nothing in the project or in an export.
75	- The slot's caption says what the scope reads: "Rec. 709 · encoded", the picture's own encoded values.
76	- In an HDR (HLG) project the caption reads "Rec. 2100 HLG", and the targets and the skin line are redrawn for that colour space, with the skin line at 139.9°. With **Show SDR Version** on, the scope reads that SDR picture as it would in an SDR project. See [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/).
77	- The scope is a 224 pt square. If the preview area is too short for both slots, it shrinks with them and stays square. Under 360 pt tall, only the top slot shows.
78	
79	## With an agent
80	
81	`render_frame` measures a frame's vectorscope as numbers when an agent passes `vectorscope: true`, which is off by default. `vectorscope_zoom` chooses 1, 2 or 4, and is 1 unless set. The reply says what share of the frame is neutral and, at 2 and 4, what share lies off the plot. The counts, the targets and the skin line's angle go to a `.vectorscope.json` file beside the image. None of this changes a slot's zoom in the panel. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
82

3	description: "Read brightness and each colour channel across the frame, and find where highlights and shadows clip."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The Waveform shows how bright the picture is across the frame. The Parade shows the same thing for red, green and blue separately. Both tell you where the picture is clipping, which is hard to judge by eye.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="View ▸ Scopes"
13	  keys="⌃⌘W"
14	  where="A slot's pop-up in the Scopes panel ▸ Waveform or Parade"
15	  tools="render_frame"
16	/>
17	
18	<Shot
19	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
20	  alt="The Waveform in the top slot of the Scopes panel beside the preview: a dark panel labelled 0, 50 and 100 at its left, with a white trace, red marks along its top and bottom edges, and under it the readouts Highlights clipped 1.9 % and Shadows clipped 52.7 %."
21	/>
22	
23	To see them, press <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> to open the [Scopes](/color/scopes/) panel, then choose **Waveform** or **Parade** from a slot's pop-up. A new window's top slot is already on **Waveform**. Each takes 200 points of height when the pane has room, and [shrinks to fit](/color/scopes/#when-the-pane-is-short) when it doesn't.
24	
25	In an HDR project they read differently, and [Scopes in an HDR project](/hdr/hdr-scopes/) has the scale.
26	
27	## Read the waveform
28	
29	The Waveform plots the picture's luma (Y′, its brightness). Left to right in the scope is left to right across the frame, and height is brightness, with black at the bottom and white at the top. So a bright window on the left of the shot shows as a high patch on the left of the scope.
30	
31	Lines mark 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %, with 0, 50 and 100 labelled at the left. The trace is white on a near-black background in both light and dark appearance. The brighter a point in the trace, the more pixels sit there, on a log scale, so a level only a few pixels reach still shows.
32	
33	## Read the RGB parade
34	
35	The Parade shows red, green and blue as three waveforms side by side, in that order, each tinted its own colour. Each one works like the Waveform, with the same lines and the whole width of the frame.
36	
37	Use it to see a colour cast. Something that should be neutral grey sits at the same height in all three, and a channel sitting higher or lower is pulling the picture toward or away from that colour. **Temperature** and **Tint** in [Light](/color/light/), and the [wheels](/color/wheels/), are the usual ways to bring them back in line.
38	
39	## Find clipping
40	
41	A pixel clips high at the top level, where an 8-bit file would write 255, and low at the bottom level, where it would write 0. Detail at those levels has gone flat.
42	
43	**Clip marks** are red marks on the top and bottom edges of the scope. A mark sits over every column where at least 0.5 % of the pixels clip, on the top edge for highlights and the bottom edge for shadows, so you can see where in the frame it's happening. The Parade marks each channel on its own, so one channel can clip when the others don't.
44	
45	**Readouts** under the Waveform give the share of the whole frame, for example **Highlights clipped 1.8 %** and **Shadows clipped 52.7 %**. They show "—" until a frame has been measured. The [Histogram](/color/histogram/) has the same two readouts. The Parade and the Vectorscope have none.
46	
47	The readouts count everything in the frame. A black background around a smaller clip counts as clipped shadows, so a high figure may not be a problem with your footage. To bring highlights down, try **Exposure** or **Highlights** in [Light](/color/light/).
48	
49	## With an agent
50	
51	`render_frame` measures a frame's Waveform or Parade without the panel. Pass `waveform` or `parade` as true. Both are false by default. The tool's reply says what share of pixels clips high and low, and for the Parade it gives that for each channel, which the panel doesn't show as a number.
52	
53	A JSON file next to the image holds the raw counts, in 256 × 256 bins, with the clip marks and the clipping figures. It's named `<image path>.waveform.json` or `<image path>.parade.json`, and the Parade's holds red, green and blue separately. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/).

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.

  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).

  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".

1	=== color-tab
2	---
3	title: The Color tab
4	description: Find every grading control in one place, learn what can be graded and in what order a grade applies, and grade several clips at once.
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
10	
11	Grading is how you correct a clip's colour and tone and give it a look of its own. The **Color** sub-tab of the Clip inspector holds every control for it: exposure and white balance, colour wheels, curves and looks. The settings on a clip are its grade.
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color"
15	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end', 'undo']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Open the Color tab
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select one or more clips on the timeline.
23	
24	2. Open the inspector's **Clip** tab.
25	
26	3. Choose **Color** in the row of sub-tabs.
27	
28	4. Open the section you want by clicking its header.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	<Shot
33	  name="05b-clip-color.window"
34	  alt="The editor window with a video clip selected. In the inspector on the right, the Clip tab's Color sub-tab is chosen and its Light section is open, showing nine sliders with number fields, all at zero. The Color and Wheels section headers sit below it, each reading neutral."
35	/>
36	
37	A video clip opens on **Picture**, so you choose **Color** yourself. Selecting a different clip sends the inspector back to that clip's first sub-tab. An adjustment clip has no **Picture** sub-tab, so it opens on **Color**.
38	
39	## What can be graded
40	
41	These clips can take a grade:
42	
43	- Video clips
44	- Image clips
45	- Stills (freeze frames)
46	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/), which grade everything behind them
47	
48	Text, shape, graphic and nest clips have no **Color** sub-tab. Nor does a clip from an audio-only file.
49	
50	### Mixed selections
51	
52	The sub-tab shows only when everything selected can take a grade, with one exception for sound.
53	
54	| Selected together | What happens |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| A video clip and an audio-only clip | The sub-tab stays. The grade goes only to the clips with a picture. |
57	| A video clip and a text, shape, graphic or nest clip | The sub-tab goes. Deselect the text, shape, graphic or nest clip to get it back. |
58	| A video clip and an adjustment clip | The sub-tab stays, and **Picture** goes. The Adjustment and Qualifier sections don't show, because not every clip is an adjustment clip. |
59	
60	## The sections
61	
62	The sections run down the tab in this order.
63	
64	| Section | What it's for | Shown for |
65	| --- | --- | --- |
66	| **Adjustment** | How strongly an adjustment clip's grade applies. See [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/). | Adjustment clips only |
67	| **Qualifier** | Narrowing an adjustment clip's grade to one colour or tone range. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/). | Adjustment clips only |
68	| **Light** | Exposure, white balance and tone. See [Light](/color/light/). | Every gradable clip |
69	| **Color** | Overall brightness, contrast, saturation and hue. See [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/). | Every gradable clip |
70	| **Wheels** | Pushing the shadows, middle tones and highlights toward a colour. See [Wheels](/color/wheels/). | Every gradable clip |
71	| **Curves** | Shaping tones and hues with points on a curve. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). | Every gradable clip |
72	| **Look** | A built-in look or your own LUT. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/). | Every gradable clip |
73	
74	Adjustment and Qualifier show only when every selected clip is an adjustment clip.
75	
76	### Which section opens
77	
78	Every section starts closed. If no section is open when the tab appears, it opens the first one you haven't closed yourself. Once you've opened or closed a section, Frame Job remembers that, for every clip and the next time you launch it.
79	
80	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, the sections it animates open by themselves. That doesn't change how you left them.
81	
82	### Read a section header
83	
84	A section's header sums up its state, so you can see what a clip carries without opening anything.
85	
86	| Section | The header reads |
87	| --- | --- |
88	| **Light**, **Color**, **Wheels**, **Curves** | "neutral" or "adjusted" |
89	| **Look** | "none", the look and its amount such as "Warm 80%", or "mixed" when the selected clips differ |
90	| **Qualifier** | "off", or what's on, such as "hue · sat · inverted" |
91	| **Adjustment** | The strength, such as "75%" |
92	
93	## Reset a section
94	
95	**Reset** appears in a section's header while the section differs from its default. It returns that section to neutral and touches nothing else, so resetting Light leaves Color alone. On Adjustment it puts **Strength** back to 100 %.
96	
97	To put back one control rather than a whole section, right-click its label or slider and choose **Reset to default**. It's dimmed while the row already holds its default.
98	
99	With an action selected, a section doesn't offer **Reset**. It shows **Clear** instead while the action animates any of that section's rows, and **Clear** takes the section out of the action. On a row, the right-click item reads **Set end value to default**. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
100	
101	## Grade several clips at once
102	
103	Select the clips and use the tab as you would for one. A control changes only its own value on each clip and keeps their other values, so dragging **Exposure** across three clips changes their exposure and nothing else.
104	
105	The value you set is the same on every clip. It isn't an offset from what each clip had.
106	
107	When the selected clips hold different values for a control, its row shows a **mixed** badge.
108	
109	An action belongs to one clip, so with several clips selected every control sets the clips' own values, even if one of them has an action.
110	
111	## Undo in the Color tab
112	
113	| You did this | It's one undo step named |
114	| --- | --- |
115	| Dragged a slider or typed a value | The control: **Undo Exposure**, **Undo Hue**, **Undo Strength** |
116	| Pressed a section's **Reset** | The section: **Undo Light**, **Undo Color**, **Undo Wheels**, **Undo Curves**, **Undo Look**, **Undo Adjustment**, **Undo Qualifier** |
117	| Pressed a section's **Clear** | **Undo Clear** |
118	
119	## The fixed grade order
120	
121	A grade always applies in one order, whatever order you made the changes in:
122	
123	1. **Color**: brightness, contrast, saturation and hue.
124	2. **Light**.
125	3. **Wheels**.
126	4. **Curves**: the tone curves first, then the hue curves.
127	5. **Look**.
128	
129	You can't change this order, so the same settings always give the same picture. The tab lists Light above Color, but Color acts first.
130	
131	A [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) conversion set on the media comes before all of these, and a [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) follows it, so a key reads the picture before your grade.
132	
133	## Filters around the grade
134	
135	The [filters](/effects/filters/) in the Picture sub-tab act on either side of the grade, which matters when you combine one with a grade.
136	
137	| Filter | Where it acts |
138	| --- | --- |
139	| Pixelate | Before the grade |
140	| Blur, Sharpen | After Color's four controls and before Light |
141	| Sepia, Noir, Vignette, Invert | After the Look, in the order you [stacked them](/effects/filters/#stack-and-reorder-filters) |
142	
143	So a filter such as Noir or Vignette works on the graded colour.
144	
145	[Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) leaves filters on, because they aren't part of the grade.
146	
147	## One grade everywhere
148	
149	The preview, **File ▸ Save Frame…** and every export apply a grade the same way, so what you see while grading is what you get.
150	
151	A clip you haven't graded renders exactly as it would without a grade. A neutral section does nothing to the picture.
152	
153	## Related
154	
155	- [Light](/color/light/)
156	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
157	- [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/)
158	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
159	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
160	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
161	- [Scopes](/color/scopes/)
162	=== color-section
163	---
164	title: Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue
165	description: Make overall changes to a clip's picture with the Color section's Brightness, Contrast, Saturation and Hue controls.
166	---
167	
168	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
169	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
170	
171	The Color section makes broad changes to the whole picture: brighter, punchier, more or less colourful, or every colour turned around the wheel.
172	
173	<AtAGlance
174	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Color"
175	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
176	/>
177	
178	## The Color section
179	
180	<Steps>
181	
182	1. Select the clip and open the [**Color**](/color/color-tab/) sub-tab.
183	
184	2. Open the **Color** section by clicking its header. It starts closed.
185	
186	3. Drag a slider, or type in the number field beside it.
187	
188	</Steps>
189	
190	All four controls start at 0.
191	
192	| Control | Range | Shows | What it does |
193	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
194	| **Brightness** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | Raises or lowers every level |
195	| **Contrast** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | Spreads the tones apart or pulls them together |
196	| **Saturation** | −1 to +1 | Two decimals | More or less colour overall |
197	| **Hue** | −180° to +180° | Whole degrees | Turns every colour around the colour wheel |
198	
199	**Reset** in the header clears these four as one undo step, **Undo Color**, and leaves [Light](/color/light/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
200	
201	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
202	
203	## Brightness
204	
205	**Brightness** adds the same amount to every level, so the blacks rise or fall with everything else. Use it for an overall lift of the whole picture. Frame Job has no Offset wheel, so this is the control for that job.
206	
207	To brighten the way a camera would, with black staying black, use [Exposure](/color/light/#set-the-exposure).
208	
209	## Contrast
210	
211	**Contrast** spreads the tones away from the middle or pulls them toward it. At +1 the spread doubles. At −1 every tone meets at mid-grey.
212	
213	For finer control over which tones move, use [the curves](/color/curves/).
214	
215	## Saturation
216	
217	**Saturation** gives more or less colour across the whole picture. −1 is greyscale and +1 is twice the colour.
218	
219	It moves every colour alike. To favour the muted colours and spare the strong ones, use [Vibrance](/color/light/#add-colour-with-vibrance).
220	
221	## Hue
222	
223	**Hue** turns every colour around the colour wheel by the same angle, from −180° to +180°. Its field shows whole degrees. Positive turns red toward yellow and then green.
224	
225	Each pixel's brightness is kept, and greys stay grey.
226	
227	To turn one colour and leave the others alone, use [Hue vs Hue](/color/hue-curves/).
228	
229	## With an agent
230	
231	An agent sets these four in `set_video`'s `color` object, as `brightness`, `contrast`, `saturation` and `hue`, and `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action. Any it doesn't name keep their values, and 0 means no change.
232	
233	An agent isn't held to the sliders' ranges for these four controls. `set_video` takes any finite number for them, with `hue` in degrees. [Light's controls](/color/light/#with-an-agent) are different: `set_video` won't take a value outside their ranges. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
234	
235	## Good to know
236	
237	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
238	- These four act first in the grade, before Light, even though the tab lists Light above them. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
239	- A [chroma key](/effects/chroma-key/) reads the picture before these controls, so changing them doesn't move the key.
240	- Blur and Sharpen act after these four. See [Filters around the grade](/color/color-tab/#filters-around-the-grade).
241	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), these controls grade everything behind the clip.
242	
243	## Related
244	
245	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
246	- [Light](/color/light/)
247	- [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/)
248	- [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/)
249	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
250	=== light
251	---
252	title: Light
253	description: Correct a clip's exposure and white balance, and shape its highlights, shadows, black and white points, vibrance and fade.
254	---
255	
256	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
257	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
258	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
259	
260	The Light section corrects how bright a clip is and how warm it looks, then shapes its tones. It's usually where a grade starts.
261	
262	<AtAGlance
263	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Light"
264	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
265	/>
266	
267	## The Light section
268	
269	<Steps>
270	
271	1. Select the clip and open the [**Color**](/color/color-tab/) sub-tab.
272	
273	2. Open the **Light** section by clicking its header, if it isn't open already.
274	
275	3. Drag a slider, or type in the number field beside it.
276	
277	</Steps>
278	
279	<Shot
280	  name="05b-clip-color.inspector"
281	  alt="The Color sub-tab with the Light section open. Nine rows run down it, Exposure, Temperature, Tint, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Vibrance and Fade, each a slider with a number field reading 0.00. Exposure's field shows EV, and Fade's slider sits at its left end while the others sit in the middle."
282	/>
283	
284	All nine controls start at 0, and each shows two decimals. The rows run in the order they act on the picture, so working down the list is a natural way to correct a clip.
285	
286	| Control | Range | What it does |
287	| --- | --- | --- |
288	| **Exposure** | −3 to +3 EV | Brightens or darkens in stops |
289	| **Temperature** | −1 to +1 | Warmer or cooler |
290	| **Tint** | −1 to +1 | Toward magenta or green |
291	| **Highlights** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the brighter half of the tones |
292	| **Shadows** | −1 to +1 | Lifts or lowers the darker half of the tones |
293	| **Whites** | −1 to +1 | Stretches the tones toward white, with black held |
294	| **Blacks** | −1 to +1 | Raises or deepens the dark end, with white held |
295	| **Vibrance** | −1 to +1 | Changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it |
296	| **Fade** | 0 to 1 | Lifts black and lowers white, for a washed-out film look |
297	
298	**Reset** in the header sets all nine back to 0 as one undo step, **Undo Light**, and leaves the [Color section](/color/color-section/) alone. The header reads "neutral" or "adjusted".
299	
300	With an [action](/color/animate-a-grade/) selected, every control here sets the value the action animates to, rather than the clip's own value.
301	
302	## Set the exposure
303	
304	**Exposure** brightens or darkens the picture in stops, from −3 to +3 EV. +1 doubles the light and −1 halves it.
305	
306	It works on linear light, meaning the amount of light in the scene rather than the encoded picture values, the way a camera's exposure does. So black stays black. To lift every level by the same amount, black included, use [Brightness](/color/color-section/#brightness).
307	
308	To judge exposure by measurement rather than by eye, watch the [waveform](/color/waveform-and-parade/) as you drag.
309	
310	## Set the white balance
311	
312	**Temperature** and **Tint** work on linear light, like Exposure. Both run from −1 to +1.
313	
314	| Control | Positive | Negative | At the limit |
315	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
316	| **Temperature** | Warmer: more red, less blue | Cooler: more blue, less red | At +1 red rises and blue falls by 0.3 of a stop. −1 is the reverse. |
317	| **Tint** | Toward magenta | Toward green | At +1 green falls by 0.3 of a stop, which reads as magenta. −1 raises it. |
318	
319	## Lift or lower the highlights and shadows
320	
321	**Highlights** moves the brighter half of the tones and **Shadows** the darker half. Both run from −1 to +1, and neither touches the other's half.
322	
323	At ±1 each moves its tones by up to a quarter of the full range. The move is strongest at the extreme, white for Highlights and black for Shadows, and fades to nothing at the middle of the tonal range.
324	
325	## Set the white and black points
326	
327	**Whites** stretches the tones toward white and holds black where it is. **Blacks** does the same at the other end: positive raises the dark end, negative deepens it, and white is held. Both run from −1 to +1.
328	
329	Each is a stretch of up to 15 %.
330	
331	## Add colour with Vibrance
332	
333	**Vibrance** changes saturation mostly in colours that have little of it, from −1 to +1. Colours that are already strong are left mostly alone, which is the difference from [Saturation](/color/color-section/#saturation), which moves every colour alike.
334	
335	At +1 a nearly grey colour gets about twice its saturation, and at −1 it goes grey. A fully saturated colour doesn't change at either end.
336	
337	## Fade the picture
338	
339	**Fade** lifts black and lowers white for a washed-out film look. It runs from 0 to 1 and has no negative side. At 1, black rises to 10 % and white falls to 95 %.
340	
341	## With an agent
342	
343	One `set_video` call can set any of the nine Light controls and the four [Color](/color/color-section/) controls together, in its `color` object, and it leaves the ones it doesn't name alone. Each key is its control's name in lower case, such as `exposure` or `fade`, and 0 means no change. A positive `temperature` is warmer and a positive `tint` is more magenta. `set_action_end` takes the same keys for an action.
344	
345	A `set_video` call with a value outside a Light control's range fails, rather than being pulled back to the limit as a typed number is. `set_action_end` does take such a value, and the action stops at the limit when it's drawn. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
346	
347	## Good to know
348	
349	- A number you type outside a control's range is pulled back to the nearest limit.
350	- Light acts after the Color section's four controls, even though the tab lists it first. See [The fixed grade order](/color/color-tab/#the-fixed-grade-order).
351	- On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), Light grades everything behind the clip.
352	- In an [HDR project](/hdr/dynamic-range/), Exposure works on the scene's light as HLG encodes it, so +1 still doubles the light.
353

362	=== wheels
363	---
364	title: "Wheels"
365	description: "Balance a clip's shadows, middle tones and highlights with Lift, Gamma and Gain, pushing each toward a colour and setting its brightness."
366	---
367	
368	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
369	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
370	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
371	
372	The wheels balance a picture by tone. **Lift** works on the shadows, **Gamma** on the middle tones and **Gain** on the highlights, so you can cool the shadows, warm the highlights or take a colour cast out of one part of the picture.
373	
374	<AtAGlance
375	  keys={['⌥-drag', 'Double-click']}
376	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Wheels"
377	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
378	/>
379	
380	<Shot
381	  name="05f-clip-wheels.inspector"
382	  alt="The Wheels section of the Color tab, reading adjusted, with a Reset button. Three columns, Lift, Gamma and Gain, each hold a colour disc, a strip and a number field. Lift's puck is pushed up and to the left, toward red-orange, and its field reads 0.10. Gamma is centred at 0.00. Gain's puck is centred and its field reads 0.20."
383	/>
384	
385	## The Wheels section
386	
387	<Steps>
388	
389	1. Select a video clip, an image, a still or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/). An adjustment clip's wheels grade everything behind it.
390	
391	2. Open the **Color** tab in the Clip inspector. See [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/) for which clips have it.
392	
393	3. Open **Wheels**. It starts closed, and its header reads **neutral** until a wheel moves, then **adjusted**.
394	
395	</Steps>
396	
397	Each of the three columns has a colour disc that [pushes its range toward a colour](#push-a-range-toward-a-colour), and a strip and a number field for [its brightness](#set-a-wheels-brightness). Every value starts at 0, which leaves the picture unchanged.
398	
399	The wheels apply after **Color** and **Light**, and before the [curves](/color/curves/) and the [look](/color/looks/). Their order is fixed.
400	
401	## What each wheel moves
402	
403	| Wheel | What it moves | Brightness at +1 | Brightness at −1 |
404	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
405	| **Lift** | Moves black and holds white, so it mostly affects the shadows. | Black rises to 25 %. | Everything below 20 % goes to black. |
406	| **Gamma** | Moves the middle tones and holds both ends. | A 50 % grey rises to about 71 %. | A 50 % grey falls to 25 %. |
407	| **Gain** | Moves white and holds black, so it mostly affects the highlights. | Every level is multiplied by 1.5. | Every level is halved, so white falls to 50 %. |
408	
409	A push follows the same rule. On **Lift** it tints the blacks and leaves white alone, and on **Gain** it tints the whites and leaves black alone.
410	
411	## Push a range toward a colour
412	
413	Press anywhere on a disc and drag. The direction you drag picks the hue, and the distance from the centre sets the strength. To warm the highlights, for example, drag **Gain**'s puck a little toward orange, between the red at the top of the disc and the yellow on its left.
414	
415	The square puck moves by however far the pointer moves. It doesn't jump to where you pressed, and a press with no drag changes nothing. Dragging one disc radius gives the full push, and past the rim the puck slides along the rim.
416	
417	A puck changes only that wheel's colour, never its brightness. One drag is one undo step, named after the wheel, such as **Undo Lift**.
418	
419	## Set a wheel's brightness
420	
421	The strip and the field under each disc set that wheel's master brightness, from −1 to +1. The default is 0.
422	
423	- **Click the strip** off the knob and the value jumps there.
424	- **Drag the knob** and it moves from where it stands, with no jump.
425	- **Type in the field** for an exact value. It shows two decimals and has no unit. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves it, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps the old value. A number past either end is set to −1 or 1, and anything that isn't a number is ignored.
426	
427	A drag is one undo step and so is a typed value, each named after its wheel.
428	
429	## Make a fine adjustment
430	
431	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag a puck or a strip to move at a tenth of the speed. On a strip, a press with <kbd>⌥</kbd> held moves the value relative to where it stands, with no jump.
432	
433	On a disc you can press or let go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> at any point in a drag. On a strip, letting go of <kbd>⌥</kbd> before the mouse sends the knob back under the pointer.
434	
435	The same key slows a point on a [curve](/color/curves/) and a handle on a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/).
436	
437	## Read the push
438	
439	Hover a disc to see its push as a hue angle and a strength, such as **Hue 34° · 0.25**. A centred puck reads **Neutral**.
440	
441	The angle counts from red at 0°, with green at 120° and blue at 240°. The strength runs from 0 at the centre to 1 at the rim. The push has no number field, so this is the only place in the inspector to read it as a number.
442	
443	## Wheels match the vectorscope
444	
445	Each disc is turned so that a hue sits where the [vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/) draws it. Dragging toward a colour moves the trace toward that colour.
446	
447	Red sits 103° counter-clockwise from 3 o'clock, just left of the top. Going counter-clockwise from there you'll find yellow on the left, green at the lower left, cyan near the bottom, blue on the right and magenta at the upper right. Every 75 % target on the vectorscope falls within about 12° of its place on the disc.
448	
449	## Reset the wheels
450	
451	| To reset | Do this |
452	| --- | --- |
453	| One wheel's push | Double-click its disc. The puck returns to the centre and the wheel's brightness stays. |
454	| One wheel's brightness | Double-click its strip. The value returns to 0 and the push stays. |
455	| All three wheels | Choose **Reset** in the section's header, or right-click the wheels and choose **Reset to default**. **Reset** appears once a wheel has moved, while no action is selected. |
456	
457	Each of these is one undo step, even when the first click of a double-click on the strip moved the knob. A double-click is named after its wheel, and resetting all three shows as **Undo Wheels**.
458	
459	## Grade several clips at once
460	
461	Select the clips and use the wheels as usual. Each control changes only its own values. A puck gives every selected clip that wheel's push and leaves each clip's brightness and other wheels alone. A strip or a field does the same for that wheel's brightness.
462	
463	The controls show the first clip's values. When the clips differ on any wheel, a **mixed** badge appears. One badge covers all three wheels.
464	
465	## Animate the wheels
466	
467	With an action selected, a puck, a strip or a field sets the action's end value, and the wheels ramp there from their values at the action's start. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
468	
469	While the action animates the wheels, a disc shows a hollow square at the start value and the puck in the action colour. A strip fills in the action colour from the start value. A coral mark shows the value under the playhead when it differs.
470	
471	The three wheels count as one row of the action. Moving any of them puts one [◆ in the gutter](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-row-marks) beside all three, and removing the row takes all three out of the action. Right-click them for **Remove from action N** or **Set end value to default**, or choose **Clear** in the section's header.
472	
473	## Good to know
474	
475	There's no Offset wheel. For an overall lift, use **Brightness** in the [Color section](/color/color-section/).
476	
477	## With an agent
478	
479	An agent can set the wheels with `set_video` as exact numbers, and an agent is the only way to enter a push by number. Each wheel takes a push as `x` and `y` and a brightness as `master`, all from −1 to 1. Its angles count the way the tooltip does, with red at 0° along positive `x`, and aren't turned to match the disc.
480	
481	Any wheel or value it leaves out stays as it is. Frame Job won't take a push past the rim from `set_video`, and says so rather than moving it to the rim. An action's end set with `set_action_end` is different: the value is kept, and the push stops at the rim while the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
482

502	  keys={['⌫', '⌦', 'Esc', '← → ↑ ↓']}

508	  name="05g-clip-curves.inspector"

511	
512	## The Curves section
513	
514	Select a video or picture clip, or an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/) and open **Curves**. The section starts collapsed, and its header reads "neutral" until a curve changes, then "adjusted".
515	
516	The section has three parts, from top to bottom:
517	
518	- The channel picker, which chooses the curve you're editing.
519	- The plot, a square with a 4 × 4 grid. It grows with the inspector up to 300 pt wide.
520	- The selected point's **In** and **Out** fields, and **Delete**.
521	
522	Across the plot is the level going in, from 0 at the left to 1 at the right. Up the plot is the level coming out. A thin diagonal marks a straight curve, which changes nothing.
523	
524	## The channel picker
525	
526	Six cells above the plot choose the channel you edit. Click a different cell, and any selected point is deselected.
527	
528	| Cell | What it changes |
529	| --- | --- |
530	| **Master** | All three colours together. Use it for contrast and for the black and white points. |
531	| **Red** | The red channel only. |
532	| **Green** | The green channel only. |
533	| **Blue** | The blue channel only. |
534	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue, which turns a chosen hue toward another. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
535	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat, which saturates or mutes a chosen hue. See [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/). |
536	
537	**Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** are the tone curves, and **Hue** and **Sat** are the hue curves.
538	
539	There's no separate luma curve. **Master** runs first, then each colour goes through its own channel, so a **Red** curve works on what **Master** has already done.
540	
541	The chosen cell is framed and labelled in its channel's colour. A new window starts on **Master**, and the plot stays on your channel while the window is open. The choice isn't saved with the project.
542	
543	### See which channels are changed
544	
545	A dot under a cell means that channel has been changed.
546	
547	Changed channels also show as faint lines in their own colour behind the curve you're editing. **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** show behind each other. **Hue** and **Sat** each have their own scale, so neither shows behind the other.
548	
549	## Shape the picture
550	
551	| To | Do this |
552	| --- | --- |
553	| Add contrast | On **Master**, make a gentle S: pull a point low on the curve down, and a point high on the curve up. |
554	| Set the black point | On **Master**, drag the first point right along the bottom. Everything darker than its **In** comes out black. |
555	| Set the white point | On **Master**, drag the last point left along the top. Everything brighter than its **In** comes out white. |
556	| Lift the blacks | On **Master**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
557	| Warm the shadows | On **Red**, drag the first point up the left edge. |
558	| Take out a colour cast | On the channel that's too strong, add a point in the middle of the curve and pull it down. |
559	
560	## Edit points
561	
562	A curve holds from 2 to 16 points. It runs smoothly through every point and never overshoots, so between two points it stays between their values. Past the first and last points, a tone curve stays flat.
563	
564	Each drag, nudge, deletion or typed value is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** reads **Undo Curves**.
565	
566	### Add a point
567	
568	Click the plot away from any point. Frame Job adds a point on the curve, directly above or below your click, and selects it. Keep the button down and the same press drags it.
569	
570	A double-click on the curve itself adds one point. A double-click away from the curve adds two, side by side, because the second click misses the first point.
571	
572	A 17th point beeps, and so does a click with no room left between two points.
573	
574	On a straight channel, the new point isn't saved until you move it, nudge it or type a value, so a stray click changes nothing. It stays on the plot while it's selected, and it goes when you deselect it or change channel. You can click several in a row to pin a straight curve before you bend it, and they're all saved with the first one you move.
575	
576	On a channel that already has a shape, the click saves the new point straight away. The point lies on the curve, so the picture changes very little, if at all.
577	
578	### Drag a point
579	
580	Press a point to grab it where it stands, with no jump, and drag. It stays inside the plot and can't pass its neighbours. The closest it gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.001 on a tone curve and 0.1° on a hue curve.
581	
582	You can drag the end points too.
583	
584	### Fine drag and axis lock
585	
586	Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> while you drag to move the point at a tenth of the speed.
587	
588	Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> while you drag to lock the point to one axis. It stays put until the pointer has travelled 4 pt from the press, and then whichever direction you moved further wins for the rest of the drag. Let go of <kbd>⇧</kbd> and the point follows the pointer again.
589	
590	<kbd>⌥</kbd> and <kbd>⇧</kbd> combine.
591	
592	### Nudge a point
593	
594	With a point selected, the arrow keys nudge it. Hold <kbd>⇧</kbd> to go ten times as far. Each press is one undo step.
595	
596	| Channel | Arrow key | With <kbd>⇧</kbd> |
597	| --- | --- | --- |
598	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0.01 | 0.1 |
599	| **Hue** | 1° | 10° |
600	| **Sat** | 1° across, 0.01 up and down | 10° across, 0.1 up and down |
601	
602	### In and Out fields
603	
604	The **In** and **Out** fields below the plot let you type the selected point's position. With no point selected, they're blank and disabled.
605	
606	| Channel | **In** | **Out** |
607	| --- | --- | --- |
608	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | 0 to 1, three decimals | 0 to 1, three decimals |
609	| **Hue** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | −180° to +180°, one decimal |
610	| **Sat** | 0° to 359.9°, one decimal | 0× to 2×, two decimals |
611	
612	A number outside the range goes to the nearest end of it, and an **In** past a neighbouring point stops short of that point.
613	
614	### Delete a point
615	
616	Select the point and press <kbd>⌫</kbd> or <kbd>⌦</kbd>, choose **Delete** below the plot, or double-click the point.
617	
618	A curve can't go below two points. The keys and the double-click beep, and **Delete** is greyed out.
619	
620	### Deselect a point
621	
622	Press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, or click another channel. This also hands the keyboard back to the editor.
623	
624	### The plot and the keyboard
625	
626	While a point is selected the plot has the keyboard, so:
627	
628	- The arrow keys nudge the point rather than move the playhead.
629	- <kbd>⌫</kbd> deletes the point, not the selected clip.
630	
631	Keys the plot doesn't use still reach the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> still plays.
632	
633	## Hover readout
634	
635	While the pointer is over the plot, and during a drag, a small label shows the pointer's position and the curve's value there.
636	
637	| Channel | The label reads |
638	| --- | --- |
639	| **Master**, **Red**, **Green**, **Blue** | `In 0.42 → Out 0.47` |
640	| **Hue** | `Hue 34° → +12°` |
641	| **Sat** | `Hue 120° → ×0.80` |
642	
643	There's no label outside the plot, and that includes the spectrum strip under a hue channel.
644	
645	## Reset curves
646	
647	To straighten one channel, right-click its cell in the picker and choose **Reset Master**, **Reset Red**, **Reset Green**, **Reset Blue**, **Reset Hue** or **Reset Sat**. The item is greyed out while that channel is already straight.
648	
649	To straighten all six channels, choose **Reset** in the section's header. It shows while a curve is changed, and it's one undo step. You can also right-click the plot and choose **Reset to default**.
650	
651	## Curves inside an action
652	
653	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, a curve edit goes to the action's end, so the curve animates. Any two curves animate into each other, whatever their number of points, and so does a curve and a straight line.
654	
655	The plot shows it in its own way: the action's start curve is dashed, and the edited curve and its points are in the action colour.
656	
657	To animate a curve back to neutral, right-click a cell and choose its **Reset** item, or right-click the plot and choose **Set end value to default**. Each writes a straight curve to the action's end, for the channels that aren't already straight. The section's **Reset** isn't there while the action is selected. **Clear** takes its place once the action animates curves, and removes them from the action.
658	
659	See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
660	
661	## Good to know
662	
663	With several clips selected, the plot shows the first clip's curves, and the section shows **mixed** when they differ. An edit gives every selected clip the curve you're editing, for that channel, and leaves their other channels alone.
664	
665	Selecting another clip deselects the point.
666	
667	## With an agent
668	
669	An agent writes a whole channel at once as a list of 2 to 16 points, and that list replaces the channel. Sending `null` for a channel removes its curve, and a list that changes nothing is stored as no curve.
670	
671	A drag stops at a limit, but an agent's value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
672

681	=== hue-curves
682	---
683	title: Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves
684	description: Turn one colour toward another, or saturate or mute it, without touching the rest of the picture.
685	---
686	
687	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
688	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
689	
690	The hue curves work on one colour at a time. **Hue** turns a chosen hue toward another, such as making the greens more teal. **Sat** saturates or mutes a chosen hue, such as calming a loud red. Both leave the other colours alone.
691	
692	<AtAGlance
693	  where="Clip inspector ▸ Color ▸ Curves ▸ the Hue and Sat cells"
694	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
695	/>
696	
697	## The two hue channels
698	
699	The **Hue** and **Sat** cells in the channel picker put the plot into degrees. Each channel lays the colours out across the plot, and its height says what happens to the colour at that position.
700	
701	| Cell | Curve | Across | Up | The centre line |
702	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
703	| **Hue** | Hue vs Hue | Hue, 0° to 360° | A shift, −180° to +180° | 0°, no shift |
704	| **Sat** | Hue vs Sat | Hue, 0° to 360° | A gain, 0× to 2× | 1×, unchanged |
705	
706	So a straight hue channel is a flat line across the middle, not a diagonal. It starts with two points on that line, at 0° and 180°.
707	
708	Points work as they do on any curve: click to add one, drag, nudge, type, delete and reset. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/#edit-points). A channel holds 2 to 16 points.
709	
710	The hue curves run after **Master**, **Red**, **Green** and **Blue** and before the [look](/color/looks/), so they read each colour as those curves left it. Both hue curves read that colour once, before either changes it. A **Sat** point on the greens still acts on greens you've turned teal with **Hue**.
711	
712	## The spectrum strip
713	
714	A strip under the plot shows which colour each position stands for, from 0° at the left to 360° at the right. Thin lines mark every 60°, with lines across at the quarters and a stronger line at the centre.
715	
716	| Hue | Colour |
717	| --- | --- |
718	| 0° | Red |
719	| 60° | Yellow |
720	| 120° | Green |
721	| 180° | Cyan |
722	| 240° | Blue |
723	| 300° | Magenta |
724	
725	## Hue vs Hue
726	
727	A positive shift moves a colour to the right along the strip, from red toward yellow and green. A negative shift moves it to the left. Brightness stays as it was.
728	
729	To make the greens more teal:
730	
731	<Steps>
732	
733	1. Select the clip, open the [Color tab](/color/color-tab/), open **Curves** and click the **Hue** cell.
734	
735	2. Click the plot at about 90° and again at about 150°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
736	
737	3. Press the centre line at about 120° and drag up. The label beside the pointer shows the shift, such as `Hue 120° → +30°`.
738	
739	</Steps>
740	
741	The outer points are saved with the first point you move. Without them, the shift spreads as far as the points at 0° and 180°.
742	
743	## Hue vs Sat
744	
745	Above the centre line a hue gets more saturated, and below it less. At the bottom of the plot, 0×, that hue goes grey. At the top, 2×, its saturation doubles. Saturation scales around the colour's own brightness.
746	
747	To mute the reds:
748	
749	<Steps>
750	
751	1. With **Curves** open on the clip, click the **Sat** cell.
752	
753	2. Click the plot at about 330° and again at about 30°, without dragging. These two points hold the colours either side still.
754	
755	3. Drag the point at 0°, at the left end of the centre line, down. The label beside the pointer shows the gain, such as `Hue 0° → ×0.60`.
756	
757	</Steps>
758	
759	## Hue curve safeguards
760	
761	- **A grey stays grey.** A grey has no real hue to read, so a hue curve never tints it. When a colour's strongest and weakest channels are within 2% of each other it's left alone, and the effect fades in to full strength at 6%.
762	- **Points never cross the wrap.** A point stops at 0° and 359.9°, so it can't slide round to the other end. The curve itself does wrap: its right end runs on smoothly into its left end, so a shift around red covers both ends of the plot.
763	- **Colours stay in range.** When a turned colour can't keep its brightness, it gives up some saturation rather than clip.
764	
765	## Good to know
766	
767	- The closest a point gets to a neighbour across the plot is 0.1°.
768	- **Reset Hue** and **Reset Sat** straighten one channel from the cell's right-click menu. The section's **Reset** straightens all six, the tone curves included. See [Reset curves](/color/curves/#reset-curves).
769	- The **Hue** slider in the [Color section](/color/color-section/) turns every colour at once. Hue vs Hue turns only the colours you choose.
770	- Hue curves animate inside an action as tone curves do. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
771	
772	## With an agent
773	
774	An agent writes `hue_hue` and `hue_sat` whole, each as a list of 2 to 16 hue and value pairs, and that list replaces the channel. It can place a point anywhere from 0 up to, but not including, 360. A value outside the limits gets an error and the curve stays as it was. An action's end is the exception: the value is kept, and it's moved to the nearest limit as the action plays. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
775	
776	## Related
777

779	- [Vectorscope](/color/vectorscope/)
780	- [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/)
781	- [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/)

1	=== looks
2	---
3	title: "Looks"
4	description: "Put one of eight built-in colour treatments on a clip by picking its thumbnail, set how much of it applies, and take it off again."
5	---
6	
7	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
8	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
9	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
10	
11	A look is a finished colour treatment you put on a clip in one click and then dial back to taste. It sits on top of your own grade, so it doesn't move the Light, Color, Wheels or Curves controls, and taking it off leaves them as they were.
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu="Clip ▸ Look"
15	  where="Clip tab ▸ Color ▸ Look"
16	  tools={['set_video', 'set_action_end']}
17	/>
18	
19	## Apply a look
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select one or more clips.
24	
25	2. Open the **Color** sub-tab of the [Clip tab](/color/color-tab/), and open **Look**, its last section. It starts collapsed.
26	
27	3. Click a tile.
28	
29	4. Drag [**Amount**](#amount) until the look sits right.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	<Shot
34	  name="05d-clip-look.inspector"
35	  alt="The Look section of the Color sub-tab. A 3 by 3 grid of thumbnail tiles reads None, Warm, Cool, Teal & Orange, Vivid, Faded, Vintage, Dramatic and Black & White, with Teal & Orange outlined in blue. Below the grid are the Import LUT… button and an Amount slider at 80%. The section header reads Teal & Orange 80%, beside a Reset button."
36	/>
37	
38	The look goes on every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. A clip that already had a look keeps its amount, and a clip with no look gets 100%.
39	
40	## The Look gallery
41	
42	The gallery is a 3 × 3 grid: **None** first, then the eight looks. Each tile is a [thumbnail](#live-thumbnails) of the first selected clip with that look on it, so you choose by eye. The tile of the look every selected clip shares is outlined in the accent colour, and **None** is outlined when no selected clip has a look. When the clips disagree, no tile is outlined.
43	
44	Under the grid comes an **Imported** group, if the project holds any LUTs, and then **Import LUT…**. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
45	
46	## The eight looks
47	
48	Each look is Frame Job's own, built from the same kinds of adjustment as its tone controls. Most also push a tint into the shadows, the highlights or both.
49	
50	| Look | What it does |
51	| --- | --- |
52	| **Warm** | A warmer white balance, a little more vibrance and golden highlights. |
53	| **Cool** | A cooler white balance, a touch more contrast and blue shadows. |
54	| **Teal & Orange** | Teal shadows and orange highlights, with more contrast and vibrance. |
55	| **Vivid** | More contrast and strong vibrance, with deeper blacks and brighter whites. |
56	| **Faded** | Low contrast, muted colour, softer highlights and lifted blacks, for a washed-out picture. |
57	| **Vintage** | Muted and warm, with a fade, green-tinted shadows and yellow-tinted highlights. |
58	| **Dramatic** | Darker, contrasty and desaturated, with cool shadows. |
59	| **Black & White** | All colour removed, with more contrast, brighter whites and deeper blacks. |
60	
61	## Live thumbnails
62	
63	Each tile shows what clicking it would give you. It's the real frame as an export would draw it, with that tile applied to the selected clips, at the amount they'd keep. A clip at 40% shows you every tile at 40%.
64	
65	The frame is the one at the playhead when the playhead is inside the first selected clip. Otherwise it's that clip's first frame.
66	
67	A refresh starts about 0.3 seconds after the playhead stops or an edit lands. That wait begins again each time the frame changes, so the tiles don't refresh while playback or a scrub moves through the clip. They only render while the Look section is open, so closing the section cancels any render in progress.
68	
69	The thumbnails always show the graded picture, even with [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) on.
70	
71	## Amount
72	
73	**Amount** sets how much of the look applies, from 0 to 100%. Use the slider, type in the field, or choose 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100% behind the field's chevron.
74	
75	The row only appears when every selected clip has a look. At 0% the look stays on the clip and draws nothing, so you can bring it back later at any amount.
76	
77	Amount is the one Look control that animates. Select an action and the value you set goes to the action's end, so the look fades in or out. See [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/).
78	
79	## Remove a look
80	
81	Do any one of these:
82	
83	- Click the **None** tile.
84	- Click **Reset** in the section's header. It's there when a selected clip has a look and no action is selected.
85	- Choose **Clip ▸ Look ▸ None**.
86	
87	The look comes off every selected clip as one undo step, **Look**. The rest of the grade stays.
88	
89	## Apply a look from the menu
90	
91	**Clip ▸ Look** does what the gallery does: the eight looks, then any imported LUTs, then **None**.
92	
93	A checkmark marks the look every selected clip carries, and a dash marks one that only some of them carry. **None** is checked when no selected clip has a look. No item has a keyboard shortcut.
94	
95	The menu is available when a selected clip can take a grade. If the selection also holds clips that can't, such as a title, those clips are left alone. The **Color** sub-tab doesn't show for a selection like that, so the menu is the way to reach the gallery's looks.
96	
97	## The Look summary
98	
99	The section's header tells you what's on the selection, even with the section collapsed.
100	
101	| The header reads | What it means |
102	| --- | --- |
103	| **Warm 80%** | Every selected clip has that look at that amount. A LUT shows its name, such as **Warm Print 80%**. |
104	| **none** | No selected clip has a look. |
105	| **mixed** | The selected clips differ, in their look or in its amount. |
106	
107	## Looks on stills and adjustment clips
108	
109	A look works on video, image and still clips, and on adjustment clips. The gallery and the menu don't offer one for text, shapes, graphics or nests.
110	
111	On an [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/), the look grades everything behind the clip, for as long as the clip lasts. The clip's **Strength** scales it along with the rest of its grade, and a [qualifier](/color/qualifiers/) narrows it to the colours the qualifier selects. That's also the way to put a look over a title, or over several clips at once.
112	
113	## Good to know
114	
115	- A clip has one look at a time. Picking another replaces it, whether it's a built-in look or a LUT.
116	- A look comes after Light, Color, the wheels and the curves, so it grades your corrected picture. It comes before the Sepia, Noir, Vignette and Invert [filters](/effects/filters/).
117	- With an action selected, a tile and **None** still change the clip's own look, not the action. **Reset** is hidden then, and the header shows **Clear** instead when the action animates **Amount**.
118	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) takes the look out of the preview only. Nothing about the clip changes, and an export still has the look.
119	- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies a clip's look and its amount along with the rest of its picture settings. See [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/).
120	
121	## With an agent
122	
123	An agent sets a look by its kind with `set_video`, for example `{look: {kind: "teal_orange", amount: 0.6}}`, and removes it with `{look: null}`. The kinds are `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic` and `black_white`, and `lut` for an [imported LUT](/color/luts/#with-an-agent).
124	
125	`amount` runs from 0 to 1. Left out, a clip keeps the amount it had, or takes 1 if it had no look. An amount on its own needs a clip that already has a look. A misspelt kind or an amount outside 0 to 1 gives an error and changes nothing.
126	
127	An agent can also do something the gallery can't: put a different look at an action's end with `set_action_end`. The amount animates, and a change to another look switches at the end of the action instead of blending. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/).
128	
129	## Related
130	
131	- [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/)
132	- [The Color tab](/color/color-tab/)
133	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
134	- [Animate a grade](/color/animate-a-grade/)
135	- [Copy a grade](/color/copy-a-grade/)
136	- [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/)
